The second is Christ’s table in the world, of which the Apostle says: “You cannot partake of Christ’s table and the table of demons” [Note: [Col. 0611] 1 Cor. 10]. The third is the table of the whole Trinity in heaven, of which Truth says: “That you may eat and drink at my table in the kingdom of God” [Note: [Col. 0611] Luke 22].

No one shares in this table unless they have been washed from all mortal sins. Hence the Apostle says: “We have an altar from which those who serve the tabernacle have no authority to eat” [Note: [Col. 0611] Heb. 13]. The tabernacle is the house of our flesh. Therefore fornicators, adulterers, drunkards, gluttons, and all others [Col. 0612D] who make provision for the flesh in its desires serve the tabernacle.

Indeed, the utmost caution must be employed, that we may approach the table worthily, as it is written: “When you sit at a rich man’s table, carefully consider what is set before you; put a knife to your throat, and know that you must prepare the same things” [Note: [Col. 0611] Ecclus. 31]. And this is what the prophet touches upon when he says: “Set the table; keep watch in the watchtower, eating and drinking” [Note: [Col. 0611] Isa. 21].

With discriminating reflection and diligent consideration, the dignity of this sacrament must be weighed, of which the Apostle says: “Great is the mystery of godliness: manifested in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen by angels, preached among the nations, believed in the world, taken up in glory” [Note: [Col. 0613] 1 Tim. 3.]. Here is nothing feigned, nothing debased, nothing fictitious, nothing at all obscured. “Great is this mystery,” says the Apostle. Truly great: for it is the great price of the world, a priceless price, beyond every valuation, beyond every understanding, beyond every excellence. Whatever is in it is truth, and whatever appears in it is what appears. For beneath the visible form the whole Christ is hidden: “He made darkness his hiding-place.” Thus the prophet also, speaking to him: “Truly, you are a hidden God; you are the King of Israel, the Saviour” [Note: [Col. 0613] Isa. 45.].

[Col. 0613B] First he was hidden in the bosom of the Father, from whom he descended; afterward hidden in the form of a servant which he assumed; now hidden in the sacrament which he himself instituted on this very day. We therefore apprehend the truth of the reality beneath a certain veil of appearance, beneath a certain outer rind of the sacrament. And this is perhaps what Isaiah says: “The foals of asses that work the ground shall eat mingled mash” [Note: [Col. 0613] Isa. 30.], that is, barley with chaff—namely, truth beneath a figure. Now we are fed, as it were, upon chaff and are not satisfied; but that time will come when we shall see him face to face. As it is written: “I shall be satisfied when your glory appears” [Note: [Col. 0613] Ps. 16].

Christ is he who instituted and left that most saving sacrament as a pledge and earnest of his love, and as the surety of his charity [Col. 0613C]. “This,” he says, “is my body.” Let no one, I beg, doubt here. Let him hear what Christ says; let him believe Christ rather than himself, so that his spirit may be faithful to God [Note: [Col. 0613] Ps. 77]. Let him deny himself [Note: [Col. 0613] Luke 9], and not follow the eye of human reason, because it is bleary. Let him follow Christ in faith and hope, who is truth and life. “If your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and cast it away from you” [Note: [Col. 0613] Matt. 5]. The Holy Spirit wills us to be saved in the simplicity of faith, not by the arguments of human reason; as it is written: “His discourse is with the humble” [Note: [Col. 0613] Prov. 3].

The prophet says: “Unless you believe, you shall not understand” [Note: [Col. 0613] Isa. 7]; yet faith also has knowledge, as you see plainly in Job: “I know that my Redeemer lives, and on the last day I shall rise from the earth” [Note: [Col. 0613] Job 19]. “I know,” says Martha, “that whatever you ask [Col. 0613D] of God, God will give you” [Note: [Col. 0613] John 11]. And, speaking of her brother: “I know,” she says, “that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day” [Note: [Col. 0613] Ibid.]. And Paul: “I know whom I have believed, and I am certain that he is able to keep my deposit unto that day” [Note: [Col. 0613] 2 Tim. 1].

Those who do not attend with the utmost humility and diligence to the reverence with which Christ’s flesh and blood ought to be consecrated, how devoutly handled, how holily received, and how carefully distributed, empty Christ’s Passion and mock the whole work of our redemption. For if, to use the Apostle’s [Col. 0614A] words, “the blood of goats or bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled upon the defiled, sanctify for the cleansing of the flesh,” how much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the Holy Spirit offered himself to God, cleanse our conscience to serve the living God! [Note: [Col. 0613] Heb. 9.]

I have proposed these things concerning the sacrament of the altar and the Mass because the institution of this sacrament occurred today: today, so to speak, the Mass was born. Therefore, as though on the day of its birth, Mass is celebrated with more elegant solemnity, with a multitude and variety of priests standing around, as it is written: “Appoint a solemn day amid dense throngs, even to the horn of the altar” [Note: [Col. 0613] Ps. 117]—that is, amid the multitude of priests, even to the power and efficacy of the sacrament. Therefore, you who wash feet today, see to it that the face [Col. 0614B] of the ancient transgression is washed. Otherwise you eat and drink judgment of eternal death for yourselves if you approach without discerning Christ’s body and blood.

Yet do not despair. You have Peter; you have Paul; you have the publican and the Canaanite woman; you also have that most renowned sinful woman—examples of repentance. You have Christ, the example of mercy, the fountain of grace, the inexhaustible fountain set for the washing of the sinner and the menstruous woman: may he wash us, receive us at his table, and communicate himself to us at his own table—here, as provision for the journey in this life; hereafter, as the fullness of desires—Christ Jesus, to whom be honour and glory for ages of ages. Amen.

## SERMON XIX. ON THE SAME SUPPER OF THE LORD

“The breath of our mouth, Christ the Lord, was taken captive in our sins; under his shadow we shall live” [Note: [Col. 0613] Lam. 4].

[Col. 0614C]

These are the words of Jeremiah the prophet. “The unfolding of your words gives light and gives understanding to the little ones” [Note: [Col. 0613] Ps. 118]. The Passion of Christ, which Moses had prefigured typologically now in the bronze serpent, now in the Paschal lamb, now in the red heifer, Jeremiah demonstrates by the clearest expression of words. “The breath of our mouth,” through whom we hope, through whom we speak, through whom we live, through whom we are, “was taken captive in our sins”: in ours, not his own, because he paid what he had not taken. This is what another prophet says: “You have made me labour in your iniquities” [Note: [Col. 0613] Mal. 2].

And hanging on the cross, he could say to humankind: “Your ways and your iniquities have done these things to me, so that I have become like a beast of burden with you” [Note: [Col. 0613] Ps. 72]. If you are burdened, I shall relieve you; I shall carry your burden, so that in myself I may fulfil my law, as it is written: “Bear one another’s burdens, and thus you shall fulfil the law of Christ” [Note: [Col. 0613] Gal. 6]. I shall set my back to burdens and scourges. If you have been sold under sin, I shall permit myself to be sold as a worthless slave or a lowly beast of burden, so that you may have [Col. 0615A] the price of your redemption. If you were lost through wood, through wood I shall redeem you. If you were lost or condemned through sin, I shall make myself sin, that in sin I may condemn sin.

O how great is the pride of man! O how great the humility of God! “In his humiliation,” says Isaiah, “his judgment was taken away” [Note: [Col. 0615] Isa. 53]. And he adds: “Like a sheep he was led to slaughter; and as,” etc. Thus, conversely and in a figurative manner, one whole burnt offering was offered for all: a holy and rational offering, in which are the fragrance of life, the savour of grace, and the rectitude of glory. Every ground for ingratitude has been removed from humankind.

Created but not redeemed, man used to say: “Why should I serve my Creator? What has he done for me? If he created me, he created oxen, asses, and all other things as well. What has he done for me? He spoke, and I was made.” [Col. 0615B] You can no longer say these things, wicked servant. For he endured for you plotters in their deeds, reproachers in their words, spittle, scourges, the lance, and finally death upon the cross. Now “the mouth of those who speak iniquity is stopped” [Note: [Col. 0615] Ps. 62], nor could the Lord have shown surer proofs of charity. “No one,” he says, “has greater love than that one lay down his life for his friends” [Note: [Col. 0615] John 15].

He displayed final and most consummate love both to the Father and to us, saving us and observing the Father’s command. As it is written: “I have seen an end of every perfection; your commandment is exceedingly broad” [Note: [Col. 0615] Ps. 118]. Therefore, completing the legal observances and bringing the dominion of death to an end, he says: “It is finished” [Note: [Col. 0615] John 9]. Above all things, your crucifixion makes you lovable to us, [Col. 0615C] Jesus Christ. Had he chosen another kind of death for the work of our redemption, it would have seemed less sufficient. Here the whole human being is redeemed: the head pains him, thickly pressed with thorns; the hands pain him, pierced by nails; the side pains him, harshly stretched upon the wood and pierced by the lance; the legs pain him, the feet pain him, so that he may say: “O all you who pass by the way, consider whether there is sorrow like my sorrow” [Note: [Col. 0615] Lam. 1].

Christ’s death is a work without example, love without measure, a gift without price, grace without merit. The Gentile glories in the desire of his soul; let the Christian glory in the cross of his Lord. “Far be it from me to glory except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ” [Note: [Col. 0615] Gal. 6]! Paul, the best assessor of things, considers that he knows nothing except Jesus Christ and him crucified [Note: [Col. 0615] 1 Cor. 2]. And what is so devout, [Col. 0615D] so saving, so worthy of being impressed upon memory as Christ’s crucifixion? What so slays sin, strengthens virtue, and crucifies every wickedness? For Christ fastened our sins to the cross with his own hands; and, in order to redeem wretched humankind, after a multitude of miseries he offered himself as the evening sacrifice.

Crucified, he crucified the old human being with its deeds; he crucified the world in his elect. He crucified Paul to the world, and the world to Paul. But you for whom the world [Col. 0616A] has been crucified, and you to the world—you, I say—it is fitting, and belongs spiritually to your profession, to know absolutely nothing except Jesus Christ and him crucified: “a stumbling-block to the Gentiles,” but to us and to the others who are being saved, “the power of God and the wisdom of God” [Note: [Col. 0615] Ibid.].

There are perhaps some who carry Christ’s cross in their clothing, but do not bear it in their heart or in their body. These are they who live in luxury beneath the cross of the Lord; they do not have the *tau* on their foreheads, nor do they bear the marks upon their bodies. But those who belong to Christ “have crucified their flesh with its vices and lusts” [Note: [Col. 0615] Gal. 5]. Such persons do not fear the coming of the smiting angel. Let this be our true and highest knowledge: to know Christ crucified, who was made for us by [Col. 0616B] God not only wisdom, but righteousness, sanctification, and redemption.

Truly redemption—and so abundant that he himself redeems Israel from all its iniquities. For the Passion has made propitiation for all our iniquities. Abel’s blood cries out for vengeance; Christ’s blood cries out for redemption. For this is the blood of the spotless Lamb, with which the high priest entered once into the holy places, having found eternal redemption [Note: [Col. 0615] Heb. 9]. Today the sack containing the price of our redemption was torn; the sack of our immortality in Christ was torn, so that he, surrounded by miseries, might surround us with mercy and joy. “You have torn my sackcloth,” he says, “and clothed me with joy” [Note: [Col. 0615] Ps. 29].

Wisdom wove this sack [Col. 0616C] for nine months in the Virgin’s chamber; washed it in the Jordan; wrung it in the Passion; dried it upon the cross. Thus from the sack it fashioned a glorious garment without spot or wrinkle. In this sack Christ lay hidden for thirty-two years, “working salvation in the midst of the earth” [Note: [Col. 0615] Ps. 73]. He always “made darkness his hiding-place”; certainly not only in a hiding-place, but also on the gibbet: there his strength was hidden. For if they had known Christ, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory [Note: [Col. 0615] 1 Cor. 2].

“Sons of men, how long will you be heavy of heart?” [Note: [Col. 0615] Ps. 4]. O slow ones! O blind ones! O most beastly of all beasts! Neither the flight of demons, nor the healing of diseases, nor the raising of the dead, nor the darkening of the sun, nor the splitting of rocks, nor the prediction of future things converted the hardness of the Jews to faith. Yet neither has it torn in contrition unto repentance the hearts of many [Col. 0616D] who profess Christ.

The Jews, most cruel murderers—indeed, to speak more expressly, deicides—who laid sacrilegious hands upon Christ the Lord, were not satisfied with such wickedness as to afflict the Lord upon the gibbet of the cross, unless he were also afflicted by insults and sated with reproaches. Yet he, as a man without help, is led now from Caiaphas to Pilate, now from Pilate to Herod; by him he is despised, mocked, spat upon, [Col. 0617A] scourged, crucified; and when crucified he is reviled: “Ha! You who destroy the temple of God,” etc. “If he is the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we shall believe him” [Note: [Col. 0617] Matt. 27].

What can Christ do, or what ought he to do? It is to be feared that he may come down. On one side he sees his mother weeping, whose soul the sword of the Passion has pierced; on the other side he sees the disciple standing whom he loved; he sees those mourning women who had followed from Galilee; he sees and hears Peter urging him and saying: “Be merciful [Note: [Col. 0617] Luke 18] to yourself, Lord.” He hears his adversaries reproaching him and saying: “If you are the Son of God, come down now from the cross,” etc. [Note: [Col. 0617] Ibid.]. How could he fail to come down, in order to show himself the Son of God and satisfy everyone?

“Be merciful to yourself, Lord,” says Peter; do not expose yourself to death. It is not fitting [Col. 0617B] for you, being God and Son of the living God, to die like a sinful human being. You are our adversary, Peter. “Get behind me: you do not savour the things that are of God” [Note: [Col. 0617] Matt. 16]. Do not hinder the benefit which comes from the dispensation of human redemption. “Unless a grain of wheat falling into the earth dies, it remains alone” [Note: [Col. 0617] John 12].

But you also, good Jesus, should not submit to Peter’s counsel. He will despair and deny you; therefore he advises you to mount the cross. Fulfil the measure of love; fulfil the debt of obedience. Obedience is not complete unless it extends to death. There is no whole burnt offering unless you burn the whole. You do not offer the victim properly unless you offer the victim’s tail. Where is it, Christ, that is read of you: “Having loved your own, you loved them unto the end” [Note: [Col. 0617] John 13]? If you lay down the cross before your life, where is the love [Col. 0617C] that you proclaimed: “No one has greater than this,” etc. [Note: [Col. 0617] John 15]?

The reproaches of those who revile do not move you. You shall yet answer those who reproach; they shall yet look upon him whom they pierced; you shall yet fill their faces with shame, and they shall seek you and not find you. “If you are the King of Israel,” the ungodly say, “come down now from the cross,” etc. This wicked generation seeks the sign of descent, and no sign shall be given it except the sign of Jonah—that is, the sign of resurrection. It is a greater sign that he came forth free among the dead from the sealed tomb than if he had come down from the gibbet.

Therefore fulfil this great mystery of godliness, as the Apostle says, which was hidden from the ages [Note: [Col. 0617] Col. 1.]. Fulfil the promises to the fathers; fulfil obedience to the Father [Col. 0617D]; fulfil the law. There is no other who redeems, none who saves [Note: [Col. 0617] Ps. 7]. It would be shameful for you to begin and not complete. You have already begun; from the punctures of the nails and the openings of the side now flows the blood of the grape—the purest, tested must, precious, pressed in the winepress of the Passion from the vineyard of Sorec. Now flows the oil of mercy; water and blood flow, so that from them there may be made ointment for our eyes.

Through the nail-holes I see that God is in Christ, reconciling the world to himself. [Col. 0618A] “Iron,” he says, “passed through his soul” [Note: [Col. 0617] Ps. 104], and drew near his heart, so that we may now see that in his heart the secrets of the heart lie open. Through the wounds of his body the inward parts of the mercy of our God lie open, “whereby the Dayspring from on high has visited us” [Note: [Col. 0617] Luke 1]. The prophet, who had not yet looked in through the clefts and nail-punctures, marvels and says: “Who has known the mind of the Lord, or who has been his counsellor?” [Note: [Col. 0617] Isa. 40; Rom. 11]. The lance has opened for me the Lord’s secret, of which he foretold through Isaiah: “My secret, my secret is for me” [Note: [Col. 0617] Isa. 24]. The lance opens it to me; the nail opens it to me: how sweet is the Lord!

“Under his shadow we shall live among the nations”: Christ’s shadow is Christ’s flesh. Christ’s shadow is Christ’s faith: faith overshadows me; flesh overshadowed the Virgin Mother. Yet the flesh itself in some fashion overshadows me [Col. 0618B] when I receive the reality of the flesh in the sacrament. Now we live under his shadow among the nations; the time will come when we shall live in his light among the angelic powers. Formerly we were in the shadow of death; now we are in the shadow of life. As the bride says in the Song of Songs: “I sat under the shadow of him whom I desired” [Note: [Col. 0617] Song 2].

The time will come when hope passes into possession, faith into certainty of truth, the shadow of life into light. Then we shall be able to say: “Even if we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet now we know him so no longer” [Note: [Col. 0617] 2 Cor. 5]. For then we shall see him not in the diadem with which his stepmother—or his mother—crowned him [Note: [Col. 0617] Song 3], but in the diadem with which his Father crowned him amid the splendours of the saints: as a King in his beauty, as the Only-Begotten from the Father, because he is equal to the Father. May Christ Jesus bring us to the grace [Col. 0618C] of that vision—he who was “taken captive in our sins” [Note: [Col. 0617] Lam. 4] in order to redeem us from everlasting captivity—to whom be honour and glory for ages of ages. Amen.

## SERMON XX. ON THE DAY OF THE RESURRECTION

“The sons of Jacob announced to their father, saying: ‘Your son Joseph lives and rules throughout the whole land of Egypt.’ But Jacob, as though awakened from a heavy sleep, said: ‘I shall go and see my son before I die’” [Note: [Col. 0617] Gen. 45].

The history of Joseph has often stirred and moved the hearts of many to tears; but the story has now been worn too smooth by use, and through excessive antiquity has become tedious to many. Throughout this Lent we have heard [Col. 0618D] about Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Esau, and the other ancient fathers. Hence our ears ring; but novelty is far more pleasing than antiquity. Let the new come to redeem the old; the new Tobit to enlighten the old; the new Joseph—indeed Jesus, new and making all things new—to lead the old Joseph out of Egypt. Jesus tastes sweeter to me than Joseph.

Today Christ rises from the dead, raising life in us and destroying the kingdom of death. This is Jonah, swallowed by the sea-monster and restored again to life, [Col. 0619A] who proclaims the word of preaching to the penitent [Note: [Col. 0619] Jonah 2]. This is Nehemiah, who, intending to repair Jerusalem’s walls, visits their breaches by night [Note: [Col. 0619] Ezra 2]. This is Samson, who rises at midnight and carries away the gates of the city of Gaza [Note: [Col. 0619] Judg. 16]. This is Elisha, who, though dead, raises a dead man by touch [Note: [Col. 0619] 4 Kgs. 13]. This is Elijah, who, when he had drunk from the brook on the way, the brook dried up [Note: [Col. 0619] 3 Kgs. 17], because when Christ had drunk from the brook on the way, death was swallowed up in victory. “Where, O death, is your victory?” [Note: [Col. 0619] 1 Cor. 15].

But thanks be to God, who gave us victory over sin and death, so that, just as Christ rising from the dead dies no more [Note: [Col. 0619] Rom. 6], so the Christian, rising from the death of sin and from sin, may not die again, but may have his life hidden with Christ in God.

O how true, how magnificent, was the threat of him [Col. 0619B] who said: “I shall be your death, O death” [Note: [Col. 0619] Hos. 13]! Tasting death for all, he swallowed up every dominion of death. For, as the Apostle says: “If the Spirit of Christ dwells in us, he who raised Christ from the dead shall also give life to our mortal bodies because of the Spirit dwelling in us” [Note: [Col. 0619] Rom. 8]. “Christ,” says the Apostle, “died for our offences and rose for our justification” [Note: [Col. 0619] Rom. 4].

He rose, but once and simply, so that we may rise twice. Our first resurrection is from sin, so that sin may no longer reign in us. The second will be in the body, when this mortal, animal, ignoble, earthly, muddy body is conformed to the body of Christ’s glory. Of the first resurrection it is written: “Awake, you who sleep; arise from the dead, and Christ shall enlighten you” [Note: [Col. 0619] Eph. 5]. The first is indeed desirable; but the second is more desirable, in which the double garment will be given. Therefore the Prophet says: “My soul thirsted for you; in how many ways has my flesh thirsted for you!” [Note: [Col. 0619] Ps. 62]. This is John’s word: “Blessed and holy is the one who has a part in the first resurrection” [Note: [Col. 0619] Rev. 20].

He who says, “I am the resurrection and the life” [Note: [Col. 0619] John 11], rising from the dead today, raises us into the hope of life and the certain expectation of the glory of the children of God. Therefore I shall rejoice, because this is the day on which we are commanded to rejoice. “This,” he says, “is the day which the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it” [Note: [Col. 0619] Ps. 117]. Two days ago I was consumed by sadness and grief; looking upon Christ dead, I was frozen by a certain chill of despair, [Col. 0619D] and in a manner was dead. But my heart grew warm within me. Hearing that the Lord had risen, my heart and my flesh rejoiced in the living Lord [Note: [Col. 0619] Ps. 83], whom previously I mourned as crucified and dead.

Therefore let us rejoice in God, our Jesus, and let us not fall asleep in death. For he is excessively dead and buried in a deathly sleep who does not keep watch now that the sun has risen. For the new sun rising from the underworld strikes the eyes [Col. 0620A] weighed down by the sleep of sin. This is the day that does not grow dark, for its sun shall not set again. He is the one who opens to us the day of eternity; for this reason he set once, that once he might rise above the setting, rise in our hearts, and leave none able to hide from his heat.

For it is the heat of his desire and love: Christ, by enlightening the hearts of the saints, inflames them mightily and makes them watch and keep vigil at his command. Such are those who find him. “I love those who love me; and those who watch for me in the morning shall find me” [Note: [Col. 0619] Prov. 8]. Mary Magdalene found Jesus because, in order to find him, she kept watch at the tomb while it was still dark [Note: [Col. 0619] John 20]. Do not those words of the prophet fittingly apply to her: “My soul desired you in the night; and my spirit and [Col. 0620B] mind within me watched for you in the morning” [Note: [Col. 0619] Isa. 9]? And this: “O God, my God, I watch for you from the dawn” [Note: [Col. 0619] Ps. 62].

Those who vigilantly and anxiously seek the Lord while darkness still remains, having found the Lord shall say in the rejoicing of their hearts: “The Lord is God, and he has shone upon us” [Note: [Col. 0619] Ps. 117]. “We are filled in the morning with mercy; we rejoiced and were delighted” [Note: [Col. 0619] Ps. 89]. Undoubtedly those who said, “Was not our heart burning within us while he spoke and opened the Scriptures to us?” [Note: [Col. 0619] Luke 24], rejoiced and delighted that they had found the Lord.

Christ had found them destitute of the fire of faith; he had found them like desolate coals, smoking rather than flaming. Was not this smoke, what they said: “But we had hoped that he was the one who would redeem Israel” [Note: [Col. 0619] Ibid.]? Nevertheless, [Col. 0620C] he who came to send that fire upon the earth and willed that it should burn made their hearts burn; and, as though carrying light in his hands, he permits them a little recognition of himself when they know him in the breaking of bread, and immediately he vanishes from their eyes.

There are some among you to whom this often happens: while approaching the table of the altar, you find Christ at Christ’s tomb, with Mary Magdalene, in longing and devotion, holding his feet; yet because he has not fully ascended in your hearts, you do not presume to touch him. It also often happens to you while you go from place to place: your heart burns within you concerning Jesus while he speaks to you and opens the Scriptures. For Christ has often unexpectedly revealed to you [Col. 0620D] in reading Scriptures that were formerly obscure. Thus Christ meets and reveals himself to those who love him and rejoice in his resurrection. And this is perhaps what Isaiah says: “You met him who rejoices and does righteousness; in your ways they shall remember you” [Note: [Col. 0619] Isa. 64].

Therefore let us walk in the way of God’s commandments and delight in the paths of righteousness. For today the Lord revealed the glory of his resurrection to those walking on the way; let us likewise walk today and sing in the ways of the Lord, [Col. 0621A] “for great is the glory of the Lord” [Note: [Col. 0621] Ps. 137]—that glory, I say, which he may deign to share with us, he who today rose from the shame of death into glory, Christ Jesus. To him be blessing and splendour and thanksgiving for ages of ages. Amen.

## SERMON XXI. ON THE SAME RESURRECTION

“Worthy is the Lamb who was slain to open the book and loose its seven seals” [Note: [Col. 0621] Rev. 5].

John wept in the Apocalypse because he found no one to loose the seven seals of the sealed book. For when John the Baptist, who was greater among those born of women [Note: [Col. 0621] Luke 7], had publicly judged himself unworthy to loose the strap of Christ’s sandal [Note: [Col. 0621] Luke 3], it was as [Col. 0621B] though he said: “I am not worthy to loose the seal of the book.” The seal of the book is nothing other than the fastening of the sandal. But one of the elders said to him: “Do not weep. Worthy is the Lamb who was slain to receive the book and loose its seven seals.”

This is the rolled book, as is read in the prophet [Note: [Col. 0621] Ezek. 2], written by God’s finger upon the parchment of the virginal womb: this book in which the angels read eternal delights. This book had seven seals. For God, hiding the glory of his majesty in flesh, sealed the price of our redemption as though in a little sack. Was not the assumption of mortal flesh a sack? “You have made my garment sackcloth,” he says [Note: [Col. 0621] Ps. 68]. And again: “You have torn my sackcloth and girded [Col. 0621C] me with joy” [Note: [Col. 0621] Ps. 29]. In this sack he brought precious wares: pardon of sins, advancement in virtues, reward of merits.

Divine Wisdom wove this sack for nine months; for of her it is written: “She put her hand to strong things, and her fingers grasped the spindle” [Note: [Col. 0621] Prov. 31]. He washed this sack in the Jordan, wrung it in the Passion, and dried it upon the cross. Christ’s humanity is called a book because it contains the knowledge and instruction of life. It is called a sack because in it is hidden and sealed the treasure of eternal life. Therefore the virginal dispensation, the weakness of the body, circumcision, the flight into Egypt, hunger in the wilderness, the humility of the cross, and burial, were living seals, so that his divinity could not be comprehended. Though burial is the final [Col. 0621D] seal, it nonetheless concealed and hid much of the glory of the divine majesty.

All these things Christ today loosed; he did not break them. For, having obediently fulfilled everything pertaining to the dispensation of the flesh he assumed, today he rises from the misery of humanity into the glory of divinity. For Christ had to suffer, rise from the dead, and thus enter into his glory [Note: [Col. 0621] Luke 24]. I call it his glory—indeed, ours also. For the head shall not enter by one door and the members by another. “I will,” he says, “that where I am, there also my minister may be” [Note: [Col. 0621] John 12]. Since he says, “I will,” I am assured that the Father does not deny him the desire of his lips.

[Col. 0622A] Therefore he will share the glory of his resurrection with us. For just as he died for our justification, so he rose for our glorification. Christ died once and rose once. But we, who are dead in soul and body, need a twofold resurrection. “Blessed is he who shall have a part in the first resurrection” [Note: [Col. 0621] Rev. 20]. The first resurrection is partly in the body and partly in the soul; the second is perfect in both. But “when that which is perfect has come, then that which is in part shall be done away” [Note: [Col. 0621] 1 Cor. 13]. Then the body of our humility, now deformed, shall be refashioned; then, I say, it shall be refashioned into the body of his glory. The first resurrection belongs especially to the soul; the second, to the body.

Desiring both, but the resurrection of the flesh more than that of the soul—for in it lies the perfection of glory—the Prophet says: “My soul thirsted for you; how manifoldly did my flesh long for you” [Note: [Col. 0621] Ps. 62]. The first resurrection is signified there: “The hour is coming, and now is; when it comes, the sons of God shall hear, and those who hear shall live” [Note: [Col. 0621] John 5]. It is as if he said: Those now dead to Christ and living to the world shall hear the word of the Gospel; and by believing and doing good works shall be raised from the death of sin.

Of the second you have: “The hour is coming when the dead who are in the tombs shall hear the voice of the Son of God” [Note: [Col. 0621] John 5]. This shall occur at the archangel’s voice and at the last trumpet, when Christ comes for judgment and gives to his voice a voice of power. Then the wicked shall rise to the resurrection of judgment. But the good, who through the first resurrection [Col. 0622C] have judged and justified themselves, shall rise to the resurrection of life. The righteous now judge themselves, and thus rise from the death of the soul through justification. The ungodly, fearing no dreadful judgment, still lie in their uncleannesses. As it is written, “The ungodly shall not rise in judgment, nor sinners in the counsel of the righteous” [Note: [Col. 0621] Ps. 1].

And what is the counsel of the righteous? It is the Prophet’s word: “Your justifications are my counsel” [Note: [Col. 0621] Ps. 118]. “If we judged ourselves, we should certainly not be judged. But when we are judged, we are corrected by the Lord” [Note: [Col. 0621] 1 Cor. 11], so that we are not condemned in this world without his care. From this clause it is clear that correction is of one kind voluntary and of another divine. Voluntary correction consists in fasting, tears, and lamentation; in vigils and disciplines; in the humility of obedience and observance of discipline. I would define the other kind, but that task lies before me.

The Lord strikes and scourges, now gently and mercifully, now justly and unbearably. “O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How incomprehensible are his judgments, and unsearchable his ways! For who has known the mind of the Lord, or who has been his counsellor?” [Note: [Col. 0621] Rom. 11]. “The judgments of the Lord are a great deep” [Note: [Col. 0621] Ps. 35], because in them darkness and immeasurable depth are found. Who could comprehend why the Lord chose Jacob and rejected Esau? How is it that the Jews, called by Christ, [Col. 0623A] did not follow him but persecuted him, whereas the Tyrians and Sidonians were not called and yet followed him? He cast good seed into bad ground, where he foreknew that the seed would be trampled and choked; and conversely he gathered a hundredfold fruit from barren ground.

One man, for Christ’s love, continually mortified himself with fasts, vigils, and disciplines from childhood to old age, and yet, suddenly caught in mortal sin and dying, incurred the sentence of everlasting damnation. Another, satisfying every desire and pouring himself out to every lust, an enemy of God and a despiser of his own soul, after he has rotted in his own filth, is at last made a vessel of election and set forth to others as an example of holiness and a pattern of life.

Although God’s judgments are just, their justice is hidden from us; and he, as a watchful and wise physician, acts as wonderfully as ineffably, sometimes turning infirmity into medicine. For we have seen some who were sluggish and slow in the way of God’s commandments, and as though moving backward, whose infirmities, by the dispensation of that great physician’s wisdom, “were multiplied; afterward they hastened” [Note: [Col. 0623] Ps. 15].

Since his ways are exalted above our ways and his thoughts above our thoughts, let us cast our thoughts upon him, so that our spirit may be laid up in him. For “he who is joined to God is one spirit with him” [Note: [Col. 0623] 1 Cor. 6]. Let no one fear to abandon himself and entrust himself to Christ. Let him know that he in whom he believes is able to keep his deposit [Col. 0623C] and restore it with increase. He receives what is broken and restores it whole, refashioning what is diminished into fullness, what is lowly into what is exalted, what is corruptible into incorruptibility, what is temporal into eternity, what is earthly into heavenliness, what is miserable into blessedness.

I fear his judgment, and because of my iniquity I dread his justice. Yet since he is just and merciful, his mercy triumphs over judgment. Therefore, let all of us, jointly and severally, commend ourselves to his mercy, praying that he who endured judgment for us may, on the day of dreadful judgment, receive us into the bosom of his mercy and make us participants in the eternal resurrection—Christ Jesus, to whom be honour and glory for ages of ages. Amen.

## SERMON XXII

### SUNDAY IN ALBIS—On the Three Witnesses

“Everything born of God conquers the world” [Note: [Col. 0623] 1 John 5.].

[Col. 0623D]

After the Son of God became the son of man, and was found in outward form as a man, a human being may rightly have confidence concerning the divine generation; nor does God shrink from becoming the Father of those whose brother Christ has become. For by adoption we are sons of God, as John, whose words [Col. 0624A] these are, says: “As many as received him, he gave them power to become sons of God” [Note: [Col. 0623] John 1.]. There is a conflict between us and the world. For as the world hates Christ, so it also hates those who belong to Christ. “Do not wonder,” he says, “if the world hates you: know that it hated me first” [Note: [Col. 0623] I John 3.]. Therefore we must confidently believe that those who are born of God belong to God and conquer the world. For he himself says: “Take courage, for I have conquered the world” [Note: [Col. 0623] John 16.]. We are indeed adopted by God, so that he may be the first-born among many brethren: so that, as he conquered the world, we too may conquer; so that victory over temptation may be evidence of heavenly birth. Made conformed to the image of God through adoption, we conquer the world, like him who is Son by nature. For it is written of the saints: “Through faith the saints conquered kingdoms” [Note: [Col. 0623] Heb. 11.].

Indeed, [Col. 0624B] life and victory come from faith. “The just,” he says, “lives by faith” [Note: [Col. 0623] Heb. 10.]. Peter, shepherd of Christ’s sheep, speaking of the devil as of a roaring lion, says: “Resist him, strong in faith” [Note: [Col. 0623] I Pet. 5.]. See how the testimonies of Scripture harmonize with one another. Paul says that the saints conquered kingdoms by faith. Peter says that the prince of this world must be resisted in faith. John says: “This is the victory that conquers the world: our faith.” He continues: “Who is it that conquers the world, except the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?” Does not the whole world believe this? Do not even demons believe and tremble [Note: [Col. 0623] Jas. 2.]? But faith is not present in one who confesses that he knows the Lord yet denies him by deeds. For faith without works is dead [Note: [Col. 0623] Ibid.]; nor is faith to be understood as existing unless it is in our hearts through him who is our life [Col. 0624C]. Of him it is said: “When Christ, our life, shall appear, then we too shall appear with him in glory” [Note: [Col. 0623] Col. 3.].

He continues: “This is he who came through water and blood, Jesus Christ”; and, still showing a more excellent way: “It is the Spirit,” he says, “who bears witness that Jesus is the Son of God.” Moses came in water, from which he also received his name. But this one is greater than Moses, who came not in water only, but in water and blood. John testifies that blood and water flowed from Christ’s side [Note: [Col. 0623] John 19.]. The Spirit of truth gives the third testimony: in the water of baptism, in the blood of martyrs; by the Spirit understand charity, which “has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us” [Note: [Col. 0623] Rom. 5.]. Though someone may conquer the world by baptism or martyrdom [Col. 0624D], unless he has charity, he is nothing. These three testimonies “have been made exceedingly credible” [Note: [Col. 0623] Ps. 92]; and this is through the benefit of charity, which brings all things back to unity and makes not only three but all things one. “These three,” he says, “are one,” because, as through charity Christ is all in all, so through charity all things are one in Christ.

And it should be noted that, before speaking of the three testimonies which are in heaven, he first sets down and says: “There are [Col. 0625A] three who bear witness on earth: the Spirit, the water, and the blood; and the three are one” [Note: [Col. 0625] I John 5.]. Therefore, that we may pursue each point in its proper order: the Father bears testimony in heaven, he who formerly spoke to the fathers through the prophets and in these last days has spoken to us in his Son [Note: [Col. 0625] Heb. 1.]. The Father bears testimony when he reveals his Son to us. Of this revelation Paul says: “He who set me apart from my mother’s womb and called me through his grace, that he might reveal his Son in me” [Note: [Col. 0625] Gal. 1.]. Speaking of this very revelation, the Lord says to Peter: “Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, because flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven” [Note: [Col. 0625] Matt. 16].

The Father bears testimony when, after Jesus was baptized and came up out of the water, the heavens were opened and a voice was heard from heaven saying: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased” [Col. 0625B; Note: [Col. 0625] Matt. 3.]. And at the Transfiguration: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased” [Note: [Col. 0625] Matt. 17.]. Of this voice Peter says in his Catholic Epistle: “Such a voice came down to him from the magnificent glory: ‘This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased: hear him.’ And we heard this voice brought from heaven when we were with him on the holy mountain” [Note: [Col. 0625] II Pet. 1.]. In John’s Gospel Christ says of the Father’s testimony: “The Father who sent me, he himself has borne testimony concerning me” [Note: [Col. 0625] John 5.]. And John says in his Catholic Epistle: “If,” he says, “we receive the testimony of men, the testimony of God is greater. And this is the testimony of God which is greater: that he has testified concerning his Son” [Note: [Col. 0625] I John 5.].

The Son bears testimony when by signs and works he reveals who he is [Col. 0625C]. And when he said, “I am the light of the world” [Note: [Col. 0625] John 8.], and the Pharisees said: “You bear testimony about yourself; your testimony is not true,” he answered and said: “Even if I bear testimony about myself, my testimony is true, because I know where I came from and where I am going” [Note: [Col. 0625] Ibid.]. And again: “It is written in your law that the testimony of two is true. I am the one who bears testimony about myself, and the Father who sent me bears testimony about me” [Note: [Col. 0625] Ibid.]. Again: “It is my Father who glorifies me, whom you say is our God, and you have not known him” [Note: [Col. 0625] Ibid.]. But when he says: “If I bear testimony concerning myself, my testimony is not true,” understand this as: without the Father’s testimony. Hence he immediately adds: “There is another who bears testimony concerning me.”

The Son gives testimony on the mountain by not denying the truth. Hence Paul says in the First Epistle to Timothy: “I charge you before God, who gives life to all things, and Christ Jesus, who rendered under Pontius Pilate the good confession, that you keep the commandment unstained and irreproachable” [Col. 0625D; Note: [Col. 0625] I Tim. 6.]. The Son bears testimony by rising again and, after his resurrection, manifesting himself by many proofs; he bore testimony by ascending before the eyes of those among whom he had lived [Col. 0626A]. As it is written: “And while they were looking, he was lifted up,” etc. [Note: [Col. 0625] Acts 1.].

The Holy Spirit too bore his testimony from ancient days, when he moved over the waters, sanctifying them then in order that he might afterward sanctify us in them. He bore testimony by inspiring the prophets, foretelling future things, and showing the way of the saints which had not yet been disclosed. But also at the time of our visitation God bears testimony, when, coming upon the blessed Virgin, he visits and makes her fruitful; when he scatters tongues of fire; when, in the unity of faith and in the proclamation of the one God, he unites languages.

Therefore the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit bear testimony. “And these three are one” [Note: [Col. 0625] I John 5.]: one in the nature of a single essence and in the harmony of a single attestation. [Col. 0626B] But there are three who bear testimony on earth: spirit, water, and blood. According to the opinion of those who see more keenly, everyone who lives spiritually is called “spirit.” Thus Paul says in the First Epistle to the Corinthians: “He who cleaves to God is one spirit with him” [Note: [Col. 0625] I Cor. 6.]. And John says in his Epistle: “Do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits whether they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world. By this the Spirit of God is known: every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ to have come in the flesh is from God; and every spirit that dissolves Jesus is not from God” [Note: [Col. 0625] I John 4.]. But that person dissolves Jesus who confesses him in words and denies him in works.

Water bears testimony when someone, living spiritually after baptism, preserves the innocence [Col. 0626C] which he received in regeneration; or, having fallen after baptism, washes himself in penitential water. Such a one testifies and is sanctified, because Christ is truth. The blood of martyrs also publicly confesses Christ. Thus the spirit of the righteous, the water of penitents, and the blood of martyrs bear testimony on earth that Christ is truth, crying out with one voice and one confession.

Even demons themselves, whether willing or unwilling, bear testimony to Christ. For in Matthew they cry out and say: “What have we to do with you, Jesus, Son of God? Have you come here before the time to torment us?” [Note: [Col. 0625] Matt. 8.]. And in Mark unclean spirits cry: “You are the Son of God” [Note: [Col. 0625] Mark 3.]. And the Lord sternly warned them not to make him known. Again, in the same Mark, another demon says: “What have I to do with you, Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God, do not torment me” [Col. 0626D; Note: [Col. 0625] Mark 5.]. And in Luke: “Demons came out from many, crying out and saying: ‘What have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? We know that you are the Son of God.’ And, rebuking them, he did not allow them to speak, because they knew that he was the Christ” [Note: [Col. 0625] Luke 4.].

Moreover, in the Acts of the Apostles, when the seven sons of Sceva, a chief priest, attempted to invoke the name of Jesus over demoniacs and each said: “I adjure you by the Jesus whom Paul preaches,” the unclean spirit said to them: “Jesus I know, and Paul I recognize; but who are you?” [Col. 0627A; Note: [Col. 0627] Acts 19.]. Behold: demons bearing testimony to Christ declare that they know not only Paul but Christ. Yet we, who profess the Christian name, deny by our works the faith which we profess in words. We who ought by faith to conquer the world are conquered by the world through unbelief. And what do you think that dreadful Judge will do on the day of terrible judgment when he sees us, who have been born of God through baptism, degenerating from our Father? Will he not say to us: “You are of your father the devil” [Note: [Col. 0627] John 8.]? Will he not say: “Go, accursed ones, into the eternal fire which has been prepared for the devil and the devils, or his sons” [Note: [Col. 0627] Matt. 25.]? Let us therefore beware, brethren, of that evil hearing. Let us conquer the world, lest we be conquered by it. Let us return to Christ [Col. 0627B] through repentance in faith and truth, so that Christ Jesus, who adopted us as sons, may make us sharers and heirs of eternal life—to whom be honor and glory for ages of ages. Amen.

## SERMON XXIII. ON THE ASCENSION OF THE LORD

“While they were looking, he was lifted up, and a cloud received him from their eyes” [Note: [Col. 0627] Acts 1.].

Today the shoot of the Lord has come forth in magnificence and glory, and the fruit of the earth is sublime; the fruit of the earth is the fruit of the virginal womb. Today was fulfilled that word which the Lord foretold through the Prophet: “Now I shall arise” [Note: [Col. 0627] Ps. 107], “and now I shall be exalted. I shall arise from the dead; I shall be exalted into heaven” [Note: [Col. 0627] Isa. 33.]. Today [Col. 0627C], O Christ Jesus, your seamless tunic—that is, the integrity of Christian faith—is completed and perfectly closed; for after preaching, after temptations, after miracles, after labor, after death and the shame of the cross, after the glory of the resurrection, after you had “worked salvation in the midst of the earth” [Note: [Col. 0627] Ps. 73], you at last showed yourself to be God and Lord of heaven, making the cloud your ascent and walking upon the wings of the winds [Note: [Col. 0627] Ps. 103.].

The flesh which was to go to the Father, though it had not previously been from the Father, put off every weakness through the glory of the resurrection. It girded itself with power, clothed with light as with a garment [Note: [Col. 0627] Ibid.]. For it was fitting that the Son of Man, having fulfilled the obedience for which he came, should present himself to his Father’s gaze in the adornment of fuller glory [Col. 0627D]. Daniel once foresaw this, saying: “I watched in a vision of the night, and behold, the Son of Man was coming in the clouds of heaven; he came to the Ancient of Days, who gave him power and honor and a kingdom which shall not perish” [Note: [Col. 0627] Dan. 7.].

Christ’s flesh, formerly weighed down by the mass of our mortality, after it was crowned with glory and honor and clothed with beauty and strength, ascended powerfully into the heavens. He descended into flesh, that he might teach fleshly people in the flesh and transfer them from flesh to spirit [Col. 0628A]. Hence the Apostle too says, indicating the glorification of the flesh: “And even if we knew Christ according to the flesh, yet now we know him so no longer” [Note: [Col. 0627] II Cor. 5.]. The Lord of air and heaven ascended freely and by his own authority through the air, he who had cast out from the air the prince of this world and had fastened the aerial powers to his cross. “No one ascends into heaven except the one who descended from heaven” [Note: [Col. 0627] John 3.]. For this reason he descended: that he might ascend, and that by ascending he might draw us up with himself. “When I have been lifted up from the earth,” he says, “I shall draw all things to myself” [Note: [Col. 0627] John 12.].

God was boundless and could neither grow nor ascend. Therefore, in order that he might grow, he was made a little lower than the angels. But he ascended in order that, in his ascension, he might transcend angelic dignity. The humanity and kindness of Christ appeared indeed in his birth, and his power and glory appeared in his resurrection. But we ought especially to rejoice in his ascension [Col. 0628B], in which the way of life has been opened to us, our faith strengthened, and our confidence established: that we may go where our head has passed. A head cannot exist without its members. “Father,” he says, “I will that where I am, there also my servant may be” [Note: [Col. 0627] Ibid.]. Because of his reverence the Son was heard, and the Father did not deprive him of the desire of his lips. Everywhere he ministers to us; everywhere he kindly advances the work of our salvation. “I go,” he says, “to prepare a place for you; and if I go, I shall come again to you and take you to myself” [Note: [Col. 0627] John 14.]. “For where the body is, there the eagles will be gathered” [Note: [Col. 0627] Matt. 24.]. It is Christ’s word: “No one comes to me unless my Father draws him” [Col. 0628C; Note: [Col. 0627] John 6.]; yet no one comes to the Father unless the Son draws him.

Christ’s ascension proves his resurrection; and we ought to rejoice most powerfully on that account, because the faith of one is established through the other. For who would believe the resurrection unless the ascension proved it? He appeared after the resurrection by many proofs, but the strongest proof of the resurrection was the ascension. Christ’s flesh could never have ascended into heaven unless the power of the resurrection had glorified it and made it immune and free from every burden of mortality.

In the resurrection four things are bestowed: subtlety, agility, brightness, and immortality. Christ displayed subtlety when he entered to the disciples while the doors were shut [Note: [Col. 0627] John 20.]; agility when he walked on the waters with his feet [Note: [Col. 0627] Matt. 14.]; brightness when on Mount Tabor his face shone like the sun [Note: [Col. 0627] Matt. 17.]; immortality when, having died, he rose from the dead [Col. 0628D; Note: [Col. 0627] Matt. 28.]. He displays these four together in himself when he returns to the Father and ascends to heaven with such authority.

Today the sun was raised up and the moon stood in its order, because, as Christ ascends today, the moon—that is, the Church—is established according to God’s order in holiness and religion [Col. 0629A]. All the ancients descended to the underworld. Christ descended to us and taught the ways of innocence and purity, so that through him and to him all who have lived purely and innocently may ascend. It is the Prophet’s word: “Who shall ascend the mountain of the Lord? Or who shall stand in his holy place? One innocent in hands and pure in heart” [Note: [Col. 0629] Ps. 23.]. According to the diversity of merits there is also a diversity of rewards for those who ascend the mountain of the Lord and into the tabernacle of our God. It is Christ’s word: “In my Father’s house there are many dwelling places” [Note: [Col. 0629] John 14.]. For there were also little rooms and three stories in the ark of the Lord.

Let us, I pray, brethren, lift up our hearts to God along with our hands. Let us picture and shape within our hearts the height of the throne—the throne of God and of the Lamb—the ministry of the angels who stand by, the ranks of human beings, patriarchs, and prophets, the senate of the apostles, the choirs of martyrs, and the crowns of virgins [Col. 0629B]. As we form all these things, let us aspire in longing together with him who went about offering in the Lord’s tabernacle a sacrifice of joyful shouting, singing and saying a psalm: “How beloved are your tabernacles, Lord of hosts! My soul longs for and fails for the courts of the Lord” [Note: [Col. 0629] Ps. 83.]. If our treasure is with Christ, as the Apostle says: “I know whom I have believed, and I am certain that he is able to keep my deposit unto that day” [Note: [Col. 0629] II Tim. 1.], let our heart be there where our treasure is. Let us arrange ascents in our heart; and if we cannot ascend bodily, at least let us ascend spiritually by remembrance and longing for heavenly things [Col. 0629C], like the one who says: “I remembered these things and poured out my soul within me, because I shall pass to the place of the tabernacle, even to the house of God” [Note: [Col. 0629] Ps. 41.]. And: “I remembered God and was delighted; I meditated, and my spirit failed” [Note: [Col. 0629] Ps. 76.].

What does he mean when he says, “My soul longs”? And again: “I remembered God and was delighted, and my spirit failed”? It is because, in this mortal life—or rather, in this life-giving death—we are not sufficient to comprehend or even conceive that glory which “eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has it entered into the heart of man, what things you, O God, have prepared for those who love you” [Note: [Col. 0629] I Cor. 2.]. But when God has transformed the body of our lowliness, configured to the body of his brightness [Note: [Col. 0629] Phil. 3.], then he who made all things for us will fill all things in us. And this is what the Apostle says [Col. 0629D]: “Christ who descended is himself the one who ascended, that he might fulfil all things” [Note: [Col. 0629] Eph. 4.] which he wished to fulfil: namely, birth, resurrection, and ascension. Thus, reborn from sin and raised from the death of the soul, may we rise from virtue to virtue, until the God of gods is seen in Zion. “The lawgiver will give blessing” [Note: [Col. 0629] Ps. 83], when he fills every living thing with blessing [Note: [Col. 0629] Ps. 144], when he says: “Come, blessed of my Father, receive the kingdom of God which has been prepared for you from the origin of the world” [Note: [Col. 0629] Matt. 25.].

As Christ was about to depart bodily for a time from that school of his [Col. 0630A] disciples, he bestowed upon them certain first-fruits of eternal blessing, as it is written: “And while blessing them, he was carried into heaven,” in order that he might fill all things with his blessings. He completed all his works in blessing, he who is blessed for ever: Christ Jesus, our Lord God. Amen.

## SERMON XXIV. ON THE DAY OF PENTECOST

“The charity of God has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us” [Note: [Col. 0629] Rom. 3.].

The Son of God first performed his embassy, coming to us, coming to seek and save that which was lost. But now the Holy Spirit performs his embassy to us, in order to establish us in salvation. The Son has been given to us, and the Holy Spirit also has been given to us [Col. 0630B]. Isaiah testifies that the Son has been given: “A child,” he says, “has been born to us, and a Son has been given to us” [Note: [Col. 0629] Isa. 9.]. The Apostle testifies that the Holy Spirit has been given to us: “Grace,” he says, “has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us.” God therefore gave us the Son and gave us the Holy Spirit too. And what remains to him? If I dared say it: the Lord God is excessively, more than excessively, lavish of himself. How magnificent and life-giving you are! How wonderful you are, O God, in your gifts.

“Lord, what is man that you magnify him? What is man, that you remember him, or the son of man, that you visit him?” [Note: [Col. 0629] Ps. 8.] Truly you visit him: for his visitation and consolation [Col. 0630C] you now send the Son, now the Holy Spirit, reserving yourself for him to have, possess, and enjoy eternally. You sent us your Son, Lord, not to rule but to serve. “I came,” he says, “not to be served but to serve” [Note: [Col. 0629] Matt. 20.]. Yet, if I may speak without injury to your dignity and that of your Son, your Son came in order to cleanse our filth, in order, like a rejected and lowly servant, to wash away our filth with his own hands.

Let no Christian, I pray, recoil from these words. For what dung, what sewer, what rottenness of corpses, what blood of a menstruating woman, or what vomit of an unclean dog is more foul than the conscience of a sinner? Isaiah says: “My mouth is filled with the vomit of filth” [Note: [Col. 0629] Isa. 28.]. Indeed, from the heart of the wicked, as from a muddy pool and a bubbling mass of rot, unclean thoughts exhale [Col. 0630D], and horrid abominations of sins gush forth. Do not our iniquities stink before him before whom even our acts of righteousness are unclean? If you do not believe me, hear Isaiah: “All our righteousnesses are as the cloth of a menstruating woman” [Note: [Col. 0629] Isa. 64.]. To use the Apostle’s expression: Christ, “making purification of sins,” washed us from our impurities in his blood [Note: [Col. 0629] Heb. 1.].

Since the Son had worked our salvation in the midst of the earth by his word [Note: [Col. 0629] Ps. 73], and had already ascended to the Father, it was necessary that the Holy Spirit be sent to establish what he had worked “from his temple which is in Jerusalem” [Col. 0631A; Note: [Col. 0631] Ps. 63], because from there faith had its beginning and progress.

For the adopted children whom Christ had begotten in his flesh by the word of life, that they might be some beginning of his creation [Note: [Col. 0631] Jas. 1.], were still tender and little. The Church militant on earth was still a tender and newly planted growth. Hence the bride—that is, the heavenly Church—said in the Song of Songs: “Our little sister is small and has no breasts” [Note: [Col. 0631] Song 8.]. The apostles were still such as needed milk. Therefore the Holy Spirit is sent to nourish them in the faith by which the just person lives, until each grows to a perfect man, until Christ is formed in them [Note: [Col. 0631] Gal. 4.].

The Paraclete Spirit was sent, which is interpreted “advocate,” as the nourisher [Col. 0631B] and guardian of little children, as their advocate in the cause of minors, so that in every council and court he might plead for them steadfastly and effectively before the kings and tyrants of the age. For thus the Father of orphans and Judge of widows had once foretold to them: “When you stand before kings and governors, do not think about what or how you are to answer. For it shall be given you,” etc. He adds: “For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you” [Note: [Col. 0631] Matt. 10.].

Now indeed the pagan tyrants and the Jewish rulers were raising an accusation against God’s chosen ones concerning their inheritance, which had been reddened for them with their Father’s blood and confirmed by royal privilege. The Jew curtailed the boundaries of the inheritance, saying that God was known only in Judaea [Col. 0631C; Note: [Col. 0631] Ps. 75.]. But the Gentiles—concerning whom God had foretold to his Son, “Ask of me, and I will give you the nations for your inheritance and the ends of the earth for your possession” [Note: [Col. 0631] Ps. 2.]—were making Christ, God’s Son and heir, and Christians, heirs of God and co-heirs of Christ [Note: [Col. 0631] Rom. 8.], disinherited.

Therefore today this learned interpreter of the law and lawgiver comes, and in his hand is a fiery law [Note: [Col. 0631] Deut. 3.]. He comes in fire and in tongues, so that they might speak the fiery law in fiery tongues. The Holy Spirit is fire, for love is fire. And just as fire cannot fail to burn, so the Holy Spirit cannot fail to burn and warm: “There is none who hides himself from his heat” [Note: [Col. 0631] Ps. 18.]. That great craftsman, whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem [Note: [Col. 0631] Isa. 31.], tests and confirms by this fire his vessels, which he fashioned [Col. 0631D] for the adornment of his house.

Peter was formerly a soft and clayey vessel, and gave no sound resonance; the sound of a vessel insufficiently fired was in Peter when, at the voice of a servant girl, he denied Christ for the third time [Note: [Col. 0631] Matt. 26.]. But after he was clothed with power from on high, like a vessel perfectly fired he gave forth a whole and perfect sound. For, when the chief priests and Roman emperors forbade him to proclaim the word of God, he answered under pressure: “We must obey God rather than men” [Note: [Col. 0631] Acts 5.]. Behold how the fire [Col. 0632A] of the Holy Spirit had strengthened Peter.

This fire kindles, establishes, and teaches. Fire is not diminished through sharing: though it divides according as it wills, it is not diminished. “There are divisions of graces, divisions of ministries, and divisions of operations; but one and the same [Spirit] works all these things” [Note: [Col. 0631] I Cor. 12], ever unchangeable, with whom there is “no change nor shadow of alteration” [Note: [Col. 0631] Jas. 1.]. This fire devours and consumes wood, hay, and stubble—that is, sins within us. But it tests gold and precious stones by its heat and, by testing, purifies them. This is the fire of the altar of which it is read in the Apocalypse that, when the angel had taken a golden censer, filled it with fire from the altar, and cast it upon the earth, there came thunders, sounds, voices, and lightnings [Note: [Col. 0631] Rev. 8.].

For the Angel [Col. 0632B] of great counsel filled the golden censer of his most immaculate body with this fire; and, taken up into heaven, he fulfilled what he foretold: “I came to cast fire upon the earth; and what do I desire except that it burn?” [Note: [Col. 0631] Luke 12.]

He therefore sent fire upon the earth, and there came thunders in threats, lightnings in miracles, rains in teachings, and sounds and voices in preachings. Thus there suddenly came a sound from heaven. This is the sound of which it is written: “Their sound has gone out into all the earth” [Note: [Col. 0631] Ps. 18.]. But from where came this sound? From the Lord’s harp, for which it is said: “Awake, my glory; awake, psaltery and harp” [Note: [Col. 0631] Ps. 56.]. Is there one sound there? Rather, there are many sounds. There are seven. But the eighth, which completes the diapason of the blessed, is in the octave [Col. 0632C], when Alleluia shall be sung through all the streets of Jerusalem [Note: [Col. 0631] Tob. 13.].

Do you wish to hear the seven strings of the harp, or the seven sounds in its strings? The master of this heavenly music, through Isaiah, the instrument of the Holy Spirit, connects all these seven voices in a single descent, saying: “And the spirit of wisdom and understanding shall rest upon him, the spirit of counsel and fortitude, the spirit of knowledge and piety, and the spirit of the fear of the Lord shall fill him” [Note: [Col. 0631] Isa. 11.]. The first string, the spirit of fear, gives a grave sound because, according to the Apostle’s testimony, “fear has punishment” [Note: [Col. 0631] I John 4.]. The second string is the spirit of piety, whose sound is most sweet. Of this sound Wisdom says: “My spirit is sweeter than honey” [Note: [Col. 0631] Sir. 24.]. Piety moderates the string of fear, lest it despair.

The string of knowledge follows; it is sharp and guides the string of piety [Col. 0632D], lest it go astray. Then follows the string of fortitude, which is strong and establishes the string of knowledge, lest it waver. And lest fortitude do something too excessive or immoderate, the string of counsel is added, which is subtle. And lest the deliberations of counsels vanish away in their subtleties, the string of understanding is added, which is highly discerning. The string of wisdom produces the seventh sound; it is firm and extended, sweet and strong. For “Wisdom reaches mightily from end to end and orders all things sweetly” [Col. 0633A; Note: [Col. 0633] Wis. 8.].

But as the Holy Spirit has his harmony and plays a pleasant psaltery with a harp, so the evil spirit has sounds and voices for the offense of God and the destruction of the soul. Do you wish to hear destruction? Do you wish to hear seven voices or strings, and the eighth in endless punishments and eternal torments? The voices on the devil’s harp are confused, discordant, and harsh. The first string is pride; the second envy; the third vainglory; the fourth sadness; the fifth avarice; the sixth lust; the seventh sloth. The devil began playing the harp long ago: “I shall set,” he says, “my throne in the north, and I shall be like the Most High” [Note: [Col. 0633] Isa. 14.]. He began far too high and precipitously. Therefore the strings were snapped, the harp was broken, and the throne of pestilence upon which he had planned to sit [Col. 0633B] was overthrown.

Therefore the Holy Spirit descended today in fire and in sound: in fire, so that the apostles might be able to kindle others in Christ’s love; in sound, so that in a mighty spirit they might proclaim the great deeds of God. But today there is no fire in us, no sound. You have turned the fire of the Lord’s altar into strange fire—that is, the love of God into earthly love. This is the fire of wickedness. This is the fire by which Nadab and Abihu, sons of Aaron, were devoured [Note: [Col. 0633] Num. 3.]. This is the fire with which Abimelech burned the town of Thebez [Note: [Col. 0633] Judg. 9.]. With this fire the Amalekites burned Ziklag [Note: [Col. 0633] I Sam. 30.]. For the enemy of the human race continually adds fire and the kindling of temptation to us, so that he may kindle within us and bring down the house [Col. 0633C] of God.

Of this most evil fire it is written: “Fire fell upon them, and they did not see the sun” [Note: [Col. 0633] Ps. 57.]. The fire of wickedness fell upon them, and they did not see the sun of righteousness. We were devoted to Christ’s service; but now we slacken in his way—indeed, we occupy ourselves with trifles and idleness. Certainly, according to Jerome’s testimony, idleness is the enemy of the soul. The sin of the Sodomites was idleness and abundance of bread [Note: [Col. 0633] Ezek. 16.]. The question is asked why Aegisthus became an adulterer.

> The cause is obvious: he was idle.  
> Ovid, *Remedies for Love*, 161.

> You see how idleness corrupts the inactive body,  
> and how waters stagnating without motion become foul.  
> Ibid., *Letters from Pontus*, elegy 6.

Of such people it is written: “They are not in the labor of men, and they shall not be scourged with men” [Note: [Col. 0633] Ps. 72]; indeed, they shall be scourged with demons [Col. 0633D]. We were chosen for the Lord’s portion, that we might meditate on the law of the Lord and delight in it, so that we might say with the Prophet: “How I have loved your law, O Lord! It is my meditation all day long” [Note: [Col. 0633] Ps. 118.]. At the beginning of the book it is written concerning the blessedness of the man who meditates on the law of the Lord day and night [Note: [Col. 0633] Ps. 1.]. It is written: “Cursed is everyone who does the work of God negligently” [Note: [Col. 0633] Jer. 48.]. I fear that this curse concerns those who serve God negligently and falsely. For where falsehood is, God is not; the Holy Spirit is not. For it is read that [Col. 0634A] “the Holy Spirit of discipline will flee the false person” [Note: [Col. 0633] Wis. 1.].

If the charity of God had been poured out in us, the law of God would be more welcome to us than every worldly desire. But now, having forgotten God’s law, we occupy ourselves with fabulous tales, running after vanities and false insanities. “They have told me tales,” he says, “but not like your law” [Note: [Col. 0633] Ps. 118.]. Moreover, from the time the people of Israel began to neglect God’s law and slacken in the observance of his commandments, they were immediately given into the hands of Chushan-rishathaim, into the hands of Eglon, Moab, and the Philistines. For when we cease from perseverance in the divine office, we are immediately subjected to the yoke of grievous vices and to the tyranny of evil spirits.

Dinah, Jacob’s daughter, goes out to see the entertainments of foreigners; and immediately Shechem, son of Hamor, desires, seizes, violates, and deflowers her [Note: [Col. 0633] Gen. 34; Col. 0634B]. So too the soul which goes out from the house of the Lord to the enticements of this world is seized and oppressed by an evil spirit, and, being oppressed, is defiled. Jacob sits at home and obtains the grace of his father’s blessing; Esau hunts abroad and, together with his father’s blessing, loses his birthright [Note: [Col. 0633] Gen. 27.]. Clerics today are found in the streets, not in churches. “The stones of the sanctuary,” says the prophet, “are scattered at the head of every street” [Note: [Col. 0633] Lam. 4.]. Contrary to the Lord’s prohibition, the poles by which the ark is carried are drawn out of their rings.

Therefore let us devote ourselves to reading, meditation, and prayer, “praying without ceasing,” as the Apostle says [Note: [Col. 0633] I Thess. 5.]. And in Hezekiah’s song: “Like a young swallow I shall cry, and I shall meditate like a dove” [Note: [Col. 0633] Isa. 38.]. May God, who is charity, pour his charity into our hearts, that we may serve him in holiness and righteousness before him [Col. 0634C] all the days of our life [Note: [Col. 0633] Luke 1.]. Amen.

## SERMON XXV. ON THE SAME FEAST
“Can you bind together the seven shining Pleiades? Can you tie the rhinoceros with your halter, lest they break the clods of your valleys?” [Note: [Col. 0633] Job 38, 39.]

These are the words of the Lord speaking to blessed Job and asking whether he can join and unite to himself the gifts of the sevenfold Spirit, which are signified by the seven Pleiades. Christ possessed this Spirit from eternity; and, having become man, he received the same without measure, and distributed it to others according to the measure of his gift. That he received the sevenfold Spirit is shown [Col. 0634D] by the saying of Isaiah: “Seven women shall seize one man in that day,” etc. [Note: [Col. 0633] Isa. 4.]; and, that the declaration of his words may enlighten us more fully and instruct us more plainly, he says, speaking of Christ: “The spirit of wisdom and understanding shall rest upon him, the spirit of counsel and strength, the spirit of knowledge and piety; and the spirit of the fear of the Lord shall fill him” [Note: [Col. 0633] Isa. 11.]. These are the seven eyes upon one stone, and the seven lamps in the golden lampstand, as Zechariah relates [Note: [Col. 0633] Zach. 3.].

Since the Son is from the Father, and the Holy Spirit proceeds from both, [Col. 0635A] after the Son had fulfilled the office of his embassy, it was fitting that the Holy Spirit too should be sent. Christ had indeed previously given the Holy Spirit to the apostles: the completeness of their healings openly indicated this. But today the Holy Spirit was given to him for use, for help, for consolation, for miracle-working, for the gaining of the nations, and for the salvation of all peoples. The Holy Spirit is given for cleansing, renewal, righteousness, and rejoicing. “Create in me a clean heart, O God”: behold, the cleansing of the heart. “Renew a right spirit within me”: behold, the sanctification of the soul. “Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation, and strengthen me with a princely spirit”: behold, the cleansing of the heart. “Renew a right spirit within me”: behold, renewing uprightness. [Col. 0635B] “Do not take your Holy Spirit from me” [Note: [Col. 0635] Ps. 50]: behold, the sanctification of the soul, since we cannot simultaneously be the temple of God and the temple of demons.

Having been cleansed and washed, one asks to walk in right ways, lest one return again to extraordinary deeds. One is renewed in heart through uprightness; the joy of salvation is at work; one is to be strengthened by the princely spirit. Keep your vessel in sanctification, and you have the Spirit. Do not do to your neighbour what you would not have done to yourself, and you have a right spirit. Present yourself before God and neighbour as devoutly humble, and you have the princely spirit. The right spirit is given in catechesis, the Holy Spirit in baptism, and the princely spirit in confirmation. Therefore, as many of us as were baptized in Christ have put on Christ [Note: [Col. 0635] Gal. 3]; and [Col. 0635C] we have been clothed with power from on high. Christ, who received the Spirit not by measure, gave gifts to human beings, and still does not cease to give them. “Of his fullness we have all received” [Note: [Col. 0635] John 1], and “there is none who can hide himself from his heat” [Note: [Col. 0635] Ps. 18]. “His fire is in Zion and his furnace in Jerusalem” [Note: [Col. 0635] Isa. 31]. This is the fire which Christ came to cast upon the earth. Thus today he appeared over his disciples in fiery tongues, so that they might preach the fiery law in fiery speech.

Of this fire it is read in the Apocalypse: “When the angel had filled the censer with the fire of the altar, there were lightnings, voices, and thunders” [Note: [Col. 0635] Rev. 8]. Of this fire Jeremiah says: “From on high he sent fire into my bones, and instructed me.” For the Holy Spirit dwelt fully and bodily in Christ. Yet he poured out his Spirit upon all. “I will pour out,” he says, [Col. 0635D] “of my Spirit upon all flesh” [Note: [Col. 0635] Joel 2]: he pours out and has poured in, to one more and to another less. The Apostle’s word is: “To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for profit” [Note: [Col. 0635] I Cor. 12]; and: “Each has his own gift from God: one in this manner, another in that” [Note: [Col. 0635] I Cor. 7]. And he adds: “There are varieties of graces, and varieties of ministries, and varieties of workings; but one and the same Spirit, distributing to each as he wills.”

[Col. 0636A] Because of these divisions of charisms, the Holy Spirit is signified now by fire, now by oil, now by wine, and now by water. He is fire, because he always kindles us to love; because once one has been kindled by him, one does not cease to burn—that is, to love ardently. “I came to cast fire upon the earth,” he says, “and what do I desire but that it burn?” [Note: [Col. 0635] Luke 12.] Of this fire Moses says: “Fire shall always burn upon the altar” [Note: [Col. 0635] Lev. 6]. And Jeremiah: “It became in my heart as a raging fire, shut up in my bones, and I was wearied, unable to bear it” [Note: [Col. 0635] Jer. 20].

The Holy Spirit is oil for several analogous reasons. The nature of oil is always to occupy the highest place among all liquids. So too the grace of the Holy Spirit, which through the abundance of its mercy surpasses the merits and prayers of suppliants, is more excellent than all [Col. 0636B] gifts and all good things. Oil is medicinal because it eases pains; and the Holy Spirit is truly oil, because he is the Comforter, who comforts us in all our tribulation [Note: [Col. 0635] II Cor. 1]. Oil has a nature that cannot be mixed: likewise the Holy Spirit is a fountain in which no stranger shares. Oil floats upon all waters; likewise the Holy Spirit was borne upon the waters [Note: [Col. 0635] Gen. 8].

Before Peter received the Holy Spirit, his flesh was weak: at the voice of a maidservant he was afraid and denied. But after he was clothed with power from on high, and God anointed him with the oil of his mercy, his flesh was changed by the oil; and, according to Isaiah’s word, he was given the oil of joy instead of mourning, and the mantle of praise instead of a spirit of grief. This is [Col. 0636C] the oil of gladness with which Christ was anointed above his fellows [Note: [Col. 0635] Ps. 44]. The oil was poured abundantly and overflowing upon our head, that is, Christ; but the ointment which was upon the head descended not only upon the beard, but also upon the hem of the garment [Note: [Col. 0635] Ps. 432]. This is the anointing of which John speaks in his Catholic Epistle: “The anointing which you received from God shall remain in you. And you will have no need for anyone to teach you, because his anointing will teach you concerning all things” [Note: [Col. 0635] I John 2].

Thus we have that the Holy Spirit is signified now by fire and now by oil. For the Holy Spirit was given twice to the apostles: first before the Passion, and second after the Resurrection. David too, we read, was anointed twice; and in the priestly garment [Col. 0636D] scarlet twice-dyed was applied. See how great a source of ardour there is in the apostles: it is not enough for oil to be poured in, unless the oil is heated; it is not enough to apply fire, unless the fire is kindled by the pouring in of oil. Burning with this fire, the disciples went rejoicing from the presence of the council, glorying in tribulations [Note: [Col. 0635] Acts 5]. Thus the voice of the Prince of the Apostles was this: “If you suffer for Christ, you are blessed” [Note: [Col. 0635] I Pet. 3]. “Not only,” he says, “has it been granted to you to believe in him, but also to suffer for [Col. 0637A] him” [Note: [Col. 0637] Phil. 1].

Therefore, that the Holy Spirit may bear witness to our spirit, let us venerate today’s solemnity of the Holy Spirit with our whole spirit.
