For the young man shall dwell in the Virgin, and your Son shall dwell in you [Note: [Col. 0661] Isa. 62.].

And this is what he himself says: “Come, my chosen one, and I will place my throne in thee,” that I may be with you and rest with you. There are other thrones, certainly, namely the divine spirits joined to God by great familiarity; but blessed Mary is far more closely joined to her Son, since the two are of one flesh. The Father gave the Son this prerogative, that he should be consubstantial with him; the Mother has this prerogative, that she should be consubstantial with him.

She was indeed signified by that most renowned throne of Solomon. For this she has today been called and chosen: that she may be a throne, like a lofty and exalted seat. I say exalted above [Col. 0661D] the choirs of angels. A throne, because the Spirit of God rests upon her: a throne indeed, but not a throne from which he hurls thunderbolts, pronounces terrible sentences of death, and promulgates decrees of eternal condemnation. As it is written: “From the throne of God proceed flashes of lightning, voices, and thunderings” [Note: [Col. 0661] Rev. 4.].

To use the language of civil affairs: from this throne Christ exercises a peaceful jurisdiction. For through the presence, prayers, and merits of his Mother, the Son grants pardon to captives; release to those shut up; illumination to the blind; rest to the weary; health to the sick; abundance to the needy; security to the fearful; fidelity among friends; peace among [Col. 0662A] enemies; certainty in doubts; counsel in error; consolation in tribulation; defence in war; refuge in exile; harbour in shipwreck; wisdom to the ignorant; exaltation to the humble; comfort to orphans and widows; grace to beginners and those advancing; and glory and a crown to those perfected and triumphant.

Take this sun-like body from the world, and there will be nothing but night. Take Mary from heaven, and there will be among human beings nothing but the blindness of darkness, the error of a whirlwind, and enveloping gloom.

Christ had left his Mother on earth for a time, until she might communicate to the disciples all that she had seen more intimately in her Son and long pondered in her heart; and until, according to the ancient saying, with the head of the ancient serpent crushed [Note: [Col. 0661] Gen. 3.], she might impress more deeply and firmly upon believers’ hearts faith in and love for Christ, and might present to her Son without wrinkle or blemish Christ’s Church, which she had undertaken to instruct at his ascension.

It seemed to Christ that he had not ascended wholly into heaven until he drew to himself her from whose flesh and blood he had drawn his body. Therefore Christ ardently desired to have with him that chosen vessel—I mean the Virgin’s body—in which he was well pleased, in which he found nothing that could displease the Godhead, and which he had suffused with the abundance of every virtue, the fullness of every grace, and the fragrance of every heavenly spice.

[Col. 0662B] This is she in whose womb, from diverse ingredients—divinity, flesh, and soul—that incense was wonderfully and ineffably compounded by the hand of the Holy Spirit, [Col. 0662C] which Christ, standing as high priest of good things to come, offered to God the Father as an evening sacrifice upon the altar of the cross. By reason of this fragrant incense the holy Mother of God was made fragrant and sweet in her delights. Therefore she ascended “like a little column of smoke from spices of myrrh and frankincense and every powder of the perfumer” [Note: [Col. 0661] Song 3.].

For this reason certain angelic spirits, together with other angels, did not attend blessed Mary as she passed out of the wilderness of this world—perhaps sent on behalf of those who receive the word of salvation as an inheritance [Note: [Col. 0661] Heb. 1.]—marvelling at the delights of such great fragrance and sweetness. “Who is this,” they say, “who ascends from the wilderness, abounding in delights?” [Note: [Col. 0661] Song 8.] As though they said: How could such abundance of heavenly delights be found in the wilderness of mortal life, where there is nothing but pain, labour, and affliction of spirit?

[Col. 0662D] We, who are fed upon the Lord’s good things, whom in the city of God the rush of the river makes glad [Note: [Col. 0661] Ps. 45], have such delights within us not from the torrent of pleasure but from the glory of his countenance. Let the angelic powers, I pray, cease to wonder at the delights of this wilderness. For what was once a wilderness has become a garden of delights, as Isaiah says: “He shall make her wilderness a delight and her solitude like the garden of the Lord” [Note: [Col. 0661] Isa. 51.].

I call her delights in the Virgin because she was chosen beforehand by the Lord, foretold by the prophets, desired by the patriarchs, greeted by the angel, made fruitful by the Holy Spirit; prefigured in Aaron’s rod, Gideon’s fleece, Ezekiel’s gate, [Col. 0663A] and Moses’ bush; fruitful without corruption, pregnant without burden, giving birth without pain; because she is the gate of life, the first among virgins, and at once the friend of the eternal God.

Let no angel wonder if the Mother of God is assumed in splendour and glory—she who is handmaid, sister, and bride; mother and daughter. The delights of this world are momentary and shadowy: in them what delights quickly passes away, while what torments remains without end. But “delights are at his right hand unto the end” [Note: [Col. 0663] Ps. 15.].

O how great and inestimable are those delights, which no repentance follows, no end interrupts, no care disturbs, and no suspicion accompanies! O what wisdom! O what security, to serve her who, in a blessed exchange, repays eternal and ineffable goods for the smallest and temporal things!

The Mother of God once placed her Son in a lowly manger; today she is placed by her Son upon a lofty throne. She placed her Son amid two animals; today she is placed by her Son above the angels. Once she led her Son down into Egypt; today she is transferred by her Son from the wilderness of this age into heaven. She clothed her Son in poor swaddling-clothes; today she is adorned by her Son with the robe of perpetual joy. The Son shares with her his humanity and his divinity, his eternity, brightness, and joy, so that Jesus Christ, the only-begotten of the Father, may be seen, held, and possessed by his Mother—to whom be honour and glory for ages of ages. Amen.

## SERMON XXXIV. ON THE SAME ASSUMPTION

[Col. 0663C]

Today, in the heavenly court, amid the angelic principalities and powers, there is a most solemn thanksgiving and voice of praise, because the Mother of God is assumed into heaven. We, however, ought rather to mourn than applaud, since in this valley of tears we are deprived of her presence, which was for us a common occasion of joy. Yet let our pilgrimage hope and await, through her, timely consolation. For she is assumed in order that she may draw us after her in the fragrance of her perfumes [Note: [Col. 0663] Song 1]; she goes to prepare a place for us; a faithful advocate goes before us, powerful to procure the cause of our salvation, and goes to the Son. Love will give gifts to human beings: as Mother of God, gifts of the kingdom; as Queen of the heavenly powers, possessing the sovereignty of heaven and earth. The ark of the covenant had long remained at Ashdod; but today, as David brings it back, it is received at Jerusalem with solemn rejoicing, because Mary, assumed from the valley of misery and weeping, enters the heavenly city. Truly this woman is blessed among women [Note: [Col. 0663] Luke 1], both while she receives Christ on earth and while she is received by Christ in heaven. Truly blessed is she who can safely say: “All generations shall call me blessed” [Note: [Col. 0663] Ibid.].

This is the wise virgin [Col. 0664A] who, while the foolish virgins remain outside, enters with the bridegroom into the joy of the wedding. The foolish virgins complain that their lamps are going out [Note: [Col. 0663] Matthew 25]. Of this woman it is written: “Her lamp shall not be extinguished in the night” [Note: [Col. 0663] Proverbs 31]. Because of this lamp and the wonderful light with which the Blessed Virgin was surrounded when she was assumed into heaven, the angels of light wondered and said: “Who is this that comes forth like the rising dawn, fair as the moon, chosen as the sun?” [Note: [Col. 0663] Song 6]. O how beautiful is your ascent, most beautiful of women! O how beautiful are your steps in sandals, daughter of a prince! For by that love through which he willed to be made a little lower than the angels [Note: [Col. 0663] Hebrews 2], he also willed that his Mother should be glorified above the angels.

Therefore, when today the Son drew his Mother in the fragrance of his perfumes [Col. 0664B] [Note: [Col. 0663] Song 6]—for he himself is “the fragrance of life unto life”—what do you suppose he said to her, except what her forefather the patriarch once said: “O virgin of virgins, I beseech you, look carefully, attend, and see whether this is your son whom you once wrapped in swaddling-clothes, whom you led into Egypt [Note: [Col. 0663] Matthew 2], whom you sought in Jerusalem, whom you saw bound by the Jews, scourged, spat upon, and fastened to the wood [Note: [Col. 0663] Matthew 27]—if indeed you were able, with a mother’s eyes, to behold your Son’s suffering—whom you now behold exalted, crowned with glory and honour [Note: [Col. 0663] Psalm 8], above every angelic power and above everything that can be conceived?”

O full of grace, truly today the Lord is with you, and you are with the Lord: that you may dwell and rest with him, and he may have dwelling and rest with you. For you are she [Col. 0664C] of whom he says: “This is my rest for ever and ever; here I shall dwell, for I have chosen her” [Note: [Col. 0663] Psalm 131]. Truly you were full of grace, who bore him who was full of grace and truth [Note: [Col. 0663] John 1], now receiving from him the fullness of glory and honour. When you had conceived your Son, you once sang: “My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Saviour” [Note: [Col. 0663] Luke 1]; now, received by your Son, you are able to rejoice more magnificently. Above all the daughters of Zion who rejoiced in their king, today your spirit rejoices in God your Saviour.

The branch of the Lord had become magnificent and glorious, and the fruit of your womb exalted, because Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father. After your Son, your magnificence has been raised above the heavens [Note: [Col. 0663] Psalm 5], so that he who drew his earthly [Col. 0664D] origin from your flesh does not abandon your flesh upon earth. For I believe that he who, in being born, kept intact in his mother the virginal seal, himself preserved unharmed from every mortality and corruption the virgin’s body in which, through him, the fullness of the Godhead deigned to dwell. Indeed, she who had lived wholly chaste, wholly immaculate, wholly undefiled and whole—how could she feel, or ought she to feel, what the corruption of the human body is?

She may now safely ascend into heaven, she who led an angelic life on earth; leaving peace to humankind, confirming [Col. 0665A] faith and inextinguishable charity in them. Let Adam and Eve, our parents—or rather, our destroyers—rejoice today, because as Mary enters heaven, entrance is opened to their offspring. Eve led us into misery; this woman raises us into glory. This is that strong woman whom Solomon sought rather in prophecy than in doubt when he said: “Who shall find a strong woman?” [Note: [Col. 0665] Proverbs 31]. She has overcome the sceptre of the oppressor and the rod of his burden, as in the day of Midian [Note: [Col. 0665] Isaiah 9]; through her Son she powerfully bound the strong man armed; she is the one who crushed the head of the ancient serpent.

The serpent indeed lay in wait for her heel, but did not prevail. For the prince of this world came and had nothing in her. Since the head and strength of that serpent consist in the enticement of the flesh [Col. 0665B] and the pride of the mind, she destroyed both temptations through virginity and humility. O proud one, O envious one, O malicious one, where now is the deceptive wickedness of your fraud? Lord God of hosts, who delivered your people through a woman—not, I say, Deborah, but Mary—I see that here is the serpent, here is the dragon, whom you formed for him to mock. Behold the outcome of humility. Eve’s pride took paradise from us; Mary’s humility brought us back to heaven.

But where is humility today? He who is king over all the children of pride has found countless followers. The humility both of Christ and of Mary is given over to contempt. I see those who were humble and lowly in the world finding pride in [Col. 0665C] the cloister. The Lord of the universe, whom the principalities and powers of heaven obey, chose a mother humble and poor. For Isaiah says of her [Note: [Col. 0665] Ch. 10]: “Arise, poor Anathol.” Consider, I beseech you, how great is the fruit of humility. Today he bestows upon his Mother heavenly riches and immeasurable, unending delights.

Let us invoke her, because he who is mighty has done great things for her [Note: [Col. 0665] Luke 1]; he who through her has worked salvation in the midst of the earth, while she pleads for us in heaven, will not cease from works of mercy. I know that whatever this Mother asks of her Son will not lack effect: she whom he chose and chose before all others on earth, whom he exalted and super-exalted in heaven, upon whom he bestowed eminence of glory and honour above every creature. She is the loving patron set before us as help amid the assaults of temptations, [Col. 0665D] amid all the straits of dangers, amid everything which human misery can fear; she is the merciful mediatrix to the Son, to whom be glory and honour for ever and ever. Amen.

## SERMON XXXV. ON THE SAME ASSUMPTION

“Jesus entered a certain village, and a woman named Martha received him into her house” [Note: [Col. 0665] Luke 10].

The question is asked what relevance this [Col. 0666A] Gospel has to the Blessed Virgin, in which the part of Mary, Lazarus’s sister, is judged the better. For what fellowship has a sinful woman with the Virgin of virgins, with the Holy One of holy women, except that they share the same name? Yet today the Church proclaims the life of the two sisters in honour of the Blessed Virgin, who displayed in herself the office of each sister.

“Jesus entered a certain village, and a woman received him.” Some say “village,” others “house.” The bodies of martyrs were impregnable strongholds; the bodies of virgins are ivory houses. For ivory contains strength and beauty; virgins also possess the fragrance of virtues and the heavenly scent of spices, as it is written: “Myrrh and liquid myrrh and cassia are from your garments; from ivory houses, from which the daughters of kings delighted [Col. 0666B] you in your honour” [Note: [Col. 0665] Psalm 44]. A common maxim says [Note: [Col. 0665] St Bernard, Sermon 2 on the Assumption]: “He guards the stronghold well who guards his body.” Yet my body, which ought to have been a stronghold, has been reduced to a worthless hut, to a dung-heap; it is no longer a house to me, but a foul tomb swarming with the uncleanness of the dead.

Certainly all my members have conspired for my destruction, so that what is written may come to pass: “A man’s enemies are those of his own household” [Note: [Col. 0665] Micah 7; Matthew 10]. My mouth condemns me, and my eye plunders my soul [Note: [Col. 0665] Lamentations 3]; my feet run toward evil against me [Note: [Col. 0665] Proverbs 1]; my hands and the remaining members prepare to surrender the stronghold to the enemy who besieges me on every side. They offer up this stronghold against me, because they compel me to serve sin [Col. 0666C]. No one freely possesses his stronghold if the desire of sin rules within it. Therefore the Apostle says: “Let not sin reign in your mortal body, that you should obey its desires” [Note: [Col. 0665] Romans 6].

I see in the strongholds of others that faith is their tower, continence their wall, patience their outer defence; reason presides over the other functions, and prudence keeps watch. These carry the mortification of the flesh about in their body, and do not fear an external siege because they bear Christ in their body. As the Apostle says: “Glorify and bear God in your body” [Note: [Col. 0665] 1 Corinthians 6].

Martha, as the elder by birth, received Christ into her house. For the active life sometimes precedes the contemplative toward salvation: “That which is spiritual is not first, but that which is natural; afterward [Col. 0666D] that which is spiritual.” Jacob loved Rachel, but Leah was given to him instead [Note: [Col. 0665] Genesis 29]. Christ commends Mary, but is received by Martha.

“Mary,” he says, “was hearing his word” [Note: [Col. 0665] Luke 10]. Christ is received by both: by Martha in the body, by Mary in the mind. But why does Martha complain? “Lord,” she says, “do you not care that my sister has left me to minister alone?” [Note: [Col. 0665] Ibid.] Certainly, in the house where Christ is received, there ought to be no murmuring and no quarrelling; nevertheless, it is devout and pleasing that Martha should complain against Mary, and not Mary against [Col. 0667A] Martha.

Yet I see some who seemed to sit with Mary at Jesus’ feet but who, desiring outward ministries, are drawn to these not by brotherly compassion but by ambition; not by charity but by greed. It is indeed good for a person to serve the brethren, but only if he does not seek administration and accepts it unwillingly. Christ’s word is: “He who is greater among you, let him be your minister” [Note: [Col. 0667] Matthew 23]. He also says: “If anyone ministers to me, my Father will honour him” [Note: [Col. 0667] John 12]. The compassion Paul had for all, and his concern for all the Churches, accrued to Paul as merit [Note: [Col. 0667] 1 Timothy 5]. A double crown is also promised to those who govern others well by serving them.

Let each person be pleased to be occupied in the ministry of the brethren, so as to enter and go out at a superior’s command; but he rejoices joyfully if he is permitted to return to Rachel’s embrace, to the delights of contemplation. For Mary chose the better part [Note: [Col. 0667] Luke 10].

There are some who display Mary’s repose in themselves, but neither love Christ nor hear his word, because they do not walk in simplicity. Some of them plunge themselves into strange meditations, wishing to inquire and know more than they ought to know. “It is not good for one who eats too much honey,” and “the searcher of majesty shall be overwhelmed by glory” [Note: [Col. 0667] Proverbs 25]. Others, who ought to be at leisure with Mary and see how sweet the Lord is, setting him always before their sight, are carried off into vanities and false insanities, and are occupied [Col. 0667C] with worldly care, or are dissolved in sloth and torpor.

But in those who perform Martha’s office, faithfulness is required in the stewardship of household affairs, compassion toward the brethren, and a more earnest disposition of humility. Of faith it is said: “Here it is required among stewards that a man be found faithful” [Note: [Col. 0667] 1 Corinthians 4], lest he share Judas’s money-bags. Let him have compassion, that with Paul he may say truly: “Who is weak, and I am not weak?” [Note: [Col. 0667] 1 Corinthians 1]. Let him show humility, that he may be the disciple of him who says: “Learn from me, because I am meek and humble of heart” [Note: [Col. 0667] Matthew 11].

The Mother of Christ fulfilled in her Son both Martha’s and Mary’s office. May she commend us to Christ by the merit of each life, he granting it, to whom be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen.

## SERMON XXXVI. ON THE SAME ASSUMPTION

[Col. 0667D]

If you consider carefully the life of the most blessed Virgin, and the care and prudence she displayed concerning her son, you will plainly be able to find both Martha and Mary in her. She is Martha when she goes into the hill-country to greet Elizabeth, pregnant and advanced in age, so that the young woman may dutifully minister to the old woman for three months. She is Martha when she wraps the Son of God and her own son in swaddling-clothes, [Col. 0668A] feeds him at her breast, and, fleeing into Egypt, hides him from Herod’s malice. She is Martha when she anxiously seeks her son in Jerusalem; when she goes with him to the wedding; when she does not depart from her son up to his Passion; when, after a mother’s sorrows and the joy of the resurrection, she accompanies her Son, about to ascend into heaven, with the eleven disciples to the Mount of Olives.

Would you see where the Virgin rests in Mary’s office? The angel had greeted her: “But Mary considered what manner of greeting this might be” [Note: [Col. 0667] Luke 1]. She is Mary in Mary’s office while the angel speaks to Joseph, while the shepherds hasten to the child, while the Magi worship, while Zacharias and Simeon prophesy. “Mary, hearing, kept all these words, pondering them in her heart” [Note: [Col. 0667] Luke 2].

Bodily exercise, which is divided among many things, [Col. 0668B] belongs to Martha; the love of God, which desires nothing besides God, belongs to Mary. The Prophet desired this one thing, this single thing, when he said: “One thing have I asked of the Lord; this will I seek” [Note: [Col. 0667] Psalm 26]. Now one thing is necessary [Note: [Col. 0667] Luke 10]; whoever chooses this one thing chooses the better part. For charity cannot fail or be taken away. Therefore Mary chose the better part, which shall not be taken from her [Note: [Col. 0667] Ibid.].

Paul, distinguishing between the things behind and those before, as it were between the toil of the active life and the delights of contemplation, chose this one thing when he said: “But, forgetting the things behind, I stretch forth to those before” [Note: [Col. 0667] Philippians 3]; as though he said: “This one thing I have retained for myself; this one thing alone I have chosen before all else. For, in comparison with contemplation, bodily exercise profits little.”

The present Gospel makes no [Col. 0668C] mention of Lazarus. Yet I believe that the house in which Christ is received belonged by hereditary right jointly to him and his sisters. Nevertheless, where the glorious Assumption of the Virgin is treated, there is no place for Lazarus. Let him lie as though sleeping among the wounded in the tombs, so that in the virginal house in which Christ is received, the service of Mary and Martha may be accepted.

Yet I see among you the roles of Mary, the roles of Martha, and also those of Lazarus being performed. For Lazarus dwells with his sisters. Some devote themselves to contemplation: behold Mary. Some faithfully and devoutly provide what is necessary for the brethren: behold Martha. Some, reflecting upon their days in bitterness of soul, groan beneath the stone of repentance [Col. 0668D]: behold Lazarus. Those delight in the one thing; these are troubled about many things; the latter are troubled concerning themselves, as a certain penitent says: “My soul was troubled concerning myself” [Note: [Col. 0667] Psalm 41].

Some are prelates or ministers: I see these, with Noah, concerned about building and governing the ark. Others are contemplatives, who with Daniel are men of desires. A third group imitate blessed Job in the humility of repentance, he who knew pain and weakness. Of these it is written: “If Noah, Daniel, and Job should be found in the city, they would be delivered by their own righteousness; but they would save neither son nor daughter” [Col. 0669A] [Note: [Col. 0669] Ezekiel 14].

The bride in the Song of Songs notes this diversity of life in a sufficiently elegant brief expression: “Arise, my beloved, my beautiful one, my dove” [Note: [Col. 0669] Song 2]. She is the beloved who tears herself from spiritual study in order to minister to Christ and his poor, lays down her life for Christ, and this is Martha’s ministry. She is beautiful who, contemplating the Lord’s glory with unveiled face, is transformed into the same image from glory to glory, as by the Spirit of the Lord [Note: [Col. 0669] 2 Corinthians 3]: and behold Mary’s repose. She is the dove who weeps and groans in the clefts of the rock [Note: [Col. 0669] Song 2], that is, as though buried in the narrowness of repentance and enclosed among stones: behold Lazarus’s broom [scope/meaning uncertain; perhaps “task” or “office”].

The Pharisee is indignant against Mary, Martha quarrels, the disciples murmur; Mary is silent, and Christ speaks for her. Mary rests, [Col. 0669B] Martha labours; Lazarus, placed in the abyss of death, cannot cry out, for “confession perishes from the dead” [Note: [Col. 0669] Ecclesiasticus 17]. Yet “deep calls to deep” [Note: [Col. 0669] Psalm 41]: the abyss of mercy calls to the abyss of iniquity. “Lazarus,” the Lord says, “come forth” [Note: [Col. 0669] John 11]. At this word he is troubled within himself, groans in spirit, weeps, and cries: “Lazarus, come forth.” Let Lazarus, I beseech you, cry out when restored to life and say: “Lord, when my spirit was distressed within me [Note: [Col. 0669] Psalm 142], you brought my soul out of hell [Note: [Col. 0669] Psalm 29]; you made known to me the ways of life; you filled me with joy in your presence” [Note: [Col. 0669] Psalm 15].

Let us also cry to heaven, to her who today ascends to her Son. Her virginity and humility redeemed us; her mercy will save us. For if you consider the length, breadth, height, [Col. 0669C] and depth of mercy in the Virgin, she ascends into heaven, penetrates hell, fills the earth, and exercises herself wonderfully and ineffably in human hearts. Through the grace which she found with her Son, may she obtain for us the Son’s grace, so that we who rejoice in the Virgin’s glory may through her glory with her Son. May he deign to grant this, who lives and reigns as God with the Father and the Holy Spirit through all ages of ages. Amen.

## SERMON XXXVII. ON ST BARTHOLOMEW

“Be prudent as serpents and simple as doves” [Note: [Col. 0669] Matthew 10].

The Teacher of truth instructs and forms us in the school [Col. 0669D] of evangelical discipline concerning what we ought to be like in doing justice and enduring injury. Prudence is required for doing good, and simplicity for suffering evil. There is good prudence or wisdom, and bad wisdom; there is the wisdom of God and the wisdom of the world. These two wisdoms are opposed and do not weigh the value of things equally.

As Scripture says: “The wisdom of God is justified by her children” [Note: [Col. 0669] Matthew 11]; but “the children of this age are more prudent in their generation than the children of light” [Note: [Col. 0669] Luke 16]. The former has proposed to regard as light the word [Col. 0670A] of the cross and death, through which it pleased God to save believers [Note: [Col. 0669] 1 Corinthians 1]. The latter, running after vanities and false insanities, judges the word of the cross to be foolishness, because “the natural man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God” [Note: [Col. 0669] 1 Corinthians 2]. For it is foolishness to him, and he cannot understand it.

The apostle James, as judge amid so great a diversity and opposition, answers: “That,” he says, “is earthly, natural, devilish; but this is first indeed chaste, then peaceable” [Note: [Col. 0669] James 3]. “Be prudent,” he says, “as serpents.” Why does he not say, “as Epicureans, as Stoics, as Peripatetics”? Because they “became vain in their thoughts, their foolish heart was darkened,” and they were given over to a reprobate mind, serving the creature rather than the Creator [Note: [Col. 0669] Romans 1]. Therefore the Lord says of them: “I shall catch [Col. 0670B] the wise in their craftiness; I shall destroy the wisdom of the wise, and reject the prudence of the prudent” [Note: [Col. 0669] 1 Corinthians 1].

And what is this wisdom, or who is the teacher of this wisdom? He indeed who teaches humanity knowledge is himself the teacher. This wisdom is the power of God and the wisdom of God, Christ Jesus, who was made for us by God not only wisdom and righteousness, but also sanctification and redemption [Note: [Col. 0669] Ibid.], because the other wisdom is only puffing-up and destruction. And what are the precepts of the master of this school? “Be prudent as serpents.” And: “Whoever wishes to come after me, let him deny himself,” etc. [Note: [Col. 0669] Luke 9]. And: “Whoever does not hate his father and mother, and even his own soul, is not worthy of me” [Note: [Col. 0669] Luke 14].

Unhappy man that I am, how shall I follow Christ? How shall I fulfil these commands? You commanded, Lord, that your commands be kept [Col. 0670C] exceedingly [Note: [Col. 0669] Psalm 118]. Alas for me, my mother! Why did you bear me as a son of sorrow and weeping, a son of eternal damnation? Why was I received upon knees? Why was I nursed at breasts? Why was I nourished for the scaffold of hellish flame? Whoever does not do these and these things cannot be my disciple. Certainly I know that to be Christ’s disciple and to be his adversary are immediate alternatives. He himself says: “Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters” [Note: [Col. 0669] Luke 11].

O good Jesus, why have you set me against you, and why have I become burdensome to myself? I have become burdensome to myself because your yoke has become heavy and unbearable to me. In the school of your Gospel I once heard: “Come to me, all you who labour and are burdened, and I [Col. 0670D] shall refresh you. For my yoke is sweet and my burden light” [Note: [Col. 0669] Matthew 11]. Moses certainly had imposed upon us a yoke which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear [Note: [Col. 0669] Acts 15]. Yet he commanded us to love father and mother, to love also a friend, and to hate an enemy [Note: [Col. 0669] Leviticus 19]. That yoke seemed more tolerable to me; and whatever may be said of love for parents or a friend, I know that I was sufficiently inclined to hatred of an enemy, for the inclinations of human beings are prone to evil from youth [Note: [Col. 0669] Genesis 8].

But now, Lord, you impose on me a yoke [Col. 0671A] which I am altogether unable to bear. Besides Moses’s yoke, other yokes were sufficient to complete my misery, yokes by which, heavily burdened, I was pressed wholly down to earth. For “the yoke of my iniquities kept watch in your hands, Lord.” I constantly bear this burden, because “my iniquities have passed over my head; as a heavy burden they have weighed upon me” [Note: [Col. 0671] Psalm 37]. I also feel another yoke, namely the rod of the oppressor and the yoke of his burden [Note: [Col. 0671] Isaiah 9]. Besides these yokes, I, wretched in mind, having despised wedding joys, bought five yokes of oxen, in the testing of which I am always found reprobate. For fivefold sensuality presses down in me the spirit that thinks many things, and thrusts down to earth the spirit that wishes to rise on high.

Because of such diverse and heavy [Col. 0671B] yokes and burdens I have become miserable and bent down unto the end [Note: [Col. 0671] Psalm 37]; and there is no one to free and raise me except you, Lord, who free those in chains [Note: [Col. 0671] Psalm 145] and raise up the crushed. Although your law seems most burdensome to me, it will nevertheless be sweet and pleasant if you grant a blessing. I know, Lord and lawgiver, that if you anointed me with the oil of your mercy, if you refreshed me with the bread of your love, in the strength of this food I would patiently endure all things. For charity bears all things, endures all things; charity is patient [Note: [Col. 0671] 1 Corinthians 13].

If you anoint me with the oil of your gladness, all things will be changed for me into joy: “the yoke shall rot away because of the oil” [Note: [Col. 0671] Isaiah 10]. The knees now weakened by fasting shall be strengthened, and my flesh shall be changed because of the oil [Note: [Col. 0671] Psalm 108]. We read, Lord, [Note: [Col. 0671] Leviticus 2], [Col. 0671C] that the fine flour to be offered to you, if baked on a griddle, in a pan, or in an oven, must be sprinkled with oil lest it be burned by the violence of the fire. Therefore anoint me, Lord, with the oil of your charity and mercy, and I shall be able to love my enemy; I shall be able not only to hate father and mother but even myself. Now I shall delight in the way of your commandments; then there will be found in me dove-like simplicity and serpentine prudence.

I believe that the dove’s simplicity is commended in sacred speech because of innocence, gentleness, and equality in the bond of fellowship. But of the serpent it is written that it was more crafty than all the animals [Note: [Col. 0671] Genesis 3]. Among its forms of prudence, one spiritually instructs and forms us: when it sees the time of old age approaching, it enters between very narrow [Col. 0671D] stones and there lays aside the cast-off skin of its old age. But if we too wish to put off the old man with his deeds, we must enter the narrowness of repentance, the narrowness of that way which leads to life, and thus put on the new man, who was created according to God.

Indeed, there the blessed apostle, whose memory is blessed today, laid aside the skin of old age, the skin of death, in order to put on the skin of glory and joy. “Skin for skin,” it says, “and everything that a man has he will give for [Col. 0672A] his soul” [Note: [Col. 0671] Job 2]. A human being gives the skin of mortification for the skin of glorification. We shall put off this skin when “this corruptible shall put on incorruption, and this mortal immortality.” And we shall receive another skin when Christ reforms the body of our humility, conformed to the body of his glory; and I shall be clothed over with a new skin, and “in my flesh I shall see God my Saviour.”

According to Jeremiah’s word, today the Ethiopian puts off his skin and the leopard its spots [Note: [Col. 0671] Jeremiah 13]. The skin which the Apostle puts off today was the skin of mortality, and therefore that of the Ethiopian. Today, apostle of God, your youth is renewed like an eagle’s [Note: [Col. 0671] Psalm 102]. Of this skin Job says [Note: [Col. 0671] Ch. 40]: “Will you fill nets with his skin, and fishermen’s huts with his head?” This is the goatskin placed in David’s bed, so that [Col. 0672B] the innocent one may escape the hand of the persecutor. Today, Lord, you have torn the apostle’s sackcloth and clothed him with joy [Note: [Col. 0671] Psalm 29].

The old Adam fell among robbers, who stripped him of the garment of innocence and glory [Note: [Col. 0671] Luke 10]; today the most valiant soldier and athlete of Christ recovers it bravely. O malice of demons! O cruelty of men! O power of God! O constancy of martyrs! Where was the apostle’s heart when he endured these straits? Certainly in Christ, in Christ’s cross and sufferings. The remembrance of Christ’s Passion made him forget his own suffering. If he were asked whether he loved his skin, whether he loved his flesh, he would answer: “I love it; no one has ever hated his own flesh” [Note: [Col. 0671] Ephesians 5], but I love Christ more than [Col. 0672C] myself. If I am now stripped, Christ will clothe me over; and this weight of my tribulation will work in me an immense weight of glory. I know whom I have believed, and I am certain that he will not lie, because he is Truth. But I suffer for Christ, and shall reign with him; and for brief and passing tribulation I confidently await an unfading crown, unending joy, and exultation.

May Jesus Christ deign to grant this to us through the merits of blessed Bartholomew, to whom be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen.

## SERMON XXXVIII. ON THE NATIVITY OF BLESSED MARY

“Wisdom has built herself a house, and has hewn out in it seven pillars” [Note: [Col. 0671] Proverbs 9].

[Col. 0672D] This Wisdom is not the wisdom of the flesh, which is hostile to God; nor the wisdom of the world, which is foolishness with God. For this wisdom, as the apostle James testifies [Note: [Col. 0671] Ch. 3], is earthly, natural, devilish; its professors are wise to do evil, but do not know how to do good. Of them the Lord says: “I shall catch the wise in their craftiness” [Note: [Col. 0671] 1 Corinthians 3], and: “I shall destroy the wisdom of the wise, and reject the prudence of the prudent” [Note: [Col. 0671] 1 Corinthians 13].

There is another wisdom, which is from above, as James says [Note: [Col. 0671] Ch. 3], first indeed chaste [Col. 0673A] and then peaceable. This is the wisdom of which we speak; this is the wisdom that built herself a house; this is Christ, the power of God and the wisdom of God. Of him the Apostle says: “Who was made for us by God wisdom and righteousness, and also sanctification and redemption” [Note: [Col. 0673] 1 Corinthians 1]. Wisdom built herself a house because Jesus Christ chose Mary’s womb as a dwelling. This is the house of a chaste breast. Solomon writes of this house: “When I enter my house, I shall find rest there” [Note: [Col. 0673] Wisdom 8]. As though he said: “I have chosen this as my dwelling, because I have chosen her.” This is the house of God and the gate of heaven.

In this Wisdom he hewed out seven pillars, namely the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit or the seven principal virtues. Four of these, concerning which philosophers long disputed and wrote, are prudence, [Col. 0673B] temperance, fortitude, and justice. There are also three others which complete the number seven, of which the philosopher had no taste: hope, faith, and charity. These are the seven pillars, these the seven graces, these the seven women who took hold of one man on that day; for by sevenfold grace she pleased God. As though seized and held fast by these manifold graces, he chose her as his dwelling. In her as in a house, as upon a throne, as in a bed, as in a sanctuary, he rested.

The celebrated throne of Solomon, of ivory and most pure gold [Note: [Col. 0673] 3 Kings 10], was a figure and sign of this Virgin. In the gold are wisdom and dignity; in the ivory, brightness, beauty, smoothness, and strength. For although she has become beautiful [Col. 0673C] and lovely, of her strength it is written: “Who shall find a strong woman?” [Note: [Col. 0673] Proverbs 31]. She is fittingly a throne because of judicial power, because he determined to sit in her, to whom all judgment is given and who judges the ends of the earth.

Because of the diversity of graces, qualities of various names are attributed to her. She is a bridal chamber because of the communion of natures, from which Christ came forth as a bridegroom from his bridal chamber [Note: [Col. 0673] Psalm 18]. She is a field because of fruitfulness: that field, namely, into which Isaac went out to meditate, which the Lord blessed, and of which it is written: “The beauty of the field is with me” [Note: [Col. 0673] Psalm 49]. Because of strength, she is the city founded by the Most High [Note: [Col. 0673] Psalm 86]; because of virginal integrity, an enclosed garden, a sealed fountain [Note: [Col. 0673] Song 4], a shut [Col. 0673D] gate, uncut Lebanon [Note: [Col. 0673] Ecclesiasticus 24]; because of holiness, the temple of God, the gate of the sanctuary, the ark of God, the sanctuary of the Holy Spirit; because of glory, the king’s hall, the chamber of spices, the fountain of gardens [Note: [Col. 0673] Song 4], the paradise of delights.

Isaiah gathers all these things into a brief compass in praise of the Virgin: “The glory of Lebanon has been given to her, the splendor of Carmel and Sharon” [Note: [Col. 0673] Isa. 35.]. Lebanon is interpreted “whiteness,” by which are indicated both the glory of her life and the honor of her chastity. Sharon is interpreted “principality” [Col. 0674A]; and she was made not only the mediatrix of God and humankind, but also princess and Queen of heaven. She was made mistress of the world, restorer of the age, destroyer of hell, glory of martyrs, honor of virgins, strength of the righteous, confidence of the fallen, hope of those who fight, joy of angels. She is the one who knew no marriage-bed in sin; and, to complete her praise, there is added to her that special prerogative: that heavenly fruitfulness was granted to her together with virginity, as Solomon testifies: “Grace upon grace is a modest and holy woman” [Note: [Col. 0673] Eccli. 26.]. O how beautiful and chaste a generation—that she is chaste and yet bears offspring—let no woman presume to claim for herself! Mary’s privilege will neither be given to another nor taken from her [Note: [Col. 0673] Luc. 10.]: no child of a Virgin except God, and no mother except a Virgin, was fitting to be named.

Therefore today Mary is born [Col. 0674B], so that Christ may be born from Mary. Let the figure of Rebecca cease: we possess the reality; we do not seek the figure. This is she whom the messenger sought for the Son of his Lord—Gabriel the archangel for the Son of God [Note: [Col. 0673] Luc. 1.]. He himself drank from her pitcher: that is, from the conformity of her virginity and of her most pure way. Let the beasts also drink, I pray; and if we cannot drink from the pitcher of virginity, let it at least be permitted us to draw from the pitcher of humility. She was pleasing because of humility; and for this reason God chose her and chose her before all others. The sex which the Lord had condemned by the sentence of cursing in Eve [Note: [Col. 0673] Gen. 3], today he fills with the grace of blessing and the oil of mercy in Mary. She is the flask of oil [Note: [Col. 0673] III Reg. 17.]; she is the golden jar containing manna of heavenly sweetness; she is Gideon’s bowl full of dew [Note: [Col. 0673] Jud. 6.]. God, intending to wet the whole threshing-floor with dew, first drenched the fleece [Col. 0674C]; and intending to redeem the world itself, he bestowed in Mary the full price of the world.

For she was filled with such great grace—the one who was to bear him who was full of grace and truth—that from her fullness we might all receive. Greeted by the angel, she went up into the hill country and greeted Elizabeth [Note: [Col. 0673] Luc. 1.]. She confidently undertakes the office of one who greets, since she already has in her womb salvation and the author of salvation: namely, him without whom there is no salvation, who gives salvation to kings and commands salvations for Jacob. John’s soul melted when Mary spoke; and, eagerly leaping to meet her with exultation, it felt the grace of the Holy Spirit, which it, though not yet born, had also perceived beforehand. Not John alone, but his parents too received from her fullness [Col. 0674D] the Spirit of prophecy, and the entire house was filled by the fragrance of the heavenly ointment.

From ancient days, according to the word of Isaiah [Note: [Col. 0673] Cap. 29.], the Lord had devised thoughts of peace; but he had concealed those thoughts from the world, though he revealed them as a secret to his prophets. Hence, although the prophet Amos [Note: [Col. 0673] Cap. 3.] said: “The Lord will do nothing unless he has first revealed it to his servants the prophets,” Isaiah nevertheless, because, according to the saying of Wisdom, it is good to keep the king’s mystery, said: “My secret is mine; my secret is mine” [Col. 0675A] [Note: [Col. 0675] Isa. 24.]. The same Isaiah [Note: [Col. 0675] Cap. 29.] says: “Your vision shall be like the words of a sealed book.” And the angel said to Daniel: “But you, Daniel, seal the book and close up the discourse until the appointed time” [Note: [Col. 0675] Cap. 12.]. This is the time which the Lord appointed for the veil to be taken from the face of Moses, for the dividing wall between us and God to be removed; this is the time of mercy, of which it is written: “For the time has come to have mercy on her; for the time has come” [Note: [Col. 0675] Psal. 101.].

“This,” says the Apostle, “is the dispensation of the mystery hidden from ages in God, so that through the Church the manifold wisdom of God may be made known to principalities and powers” [Note: [Col. 0675] Ephes. 3.]. Therefore the woman was sought and found, in whom and through whom the grace of so great a mystery is fulfilled. The ewe was sought, from whom the Lamb of God should be born, who would take away the sins of the world. For the law did not [Col. 0675B] remove sin, but increased it; the law does not take away sin but aggravates it; it does not diminish but augments it. “The law,” says the Apostle, “entered in so that transgression might abound” [Note: [Col. 0675] Rom. 5.]; and again: “Through the commandment the law produced in me every kind of concupiscence” [Note: [Col. 0675] Rom. 7.].

Therefore she who is blessed among women is chosen and born today, so that, annulling the fruit of the curse, she may bring forth the fruit of life. “On that day,” Isaiah had foretold, “the branch of the Lord shall be in magnificence and glory, and the fruit of the earth exalted” [Note: [Col. 0675] Isai. 4.]. The evil tree had produced evil fruits: namely, the lust of the flesh, original sin, a seedbed of evils, the leaven of common corruption, and the universal beginning of our ruin. Therefore, because original evil had to be healed by original good, the flesh of the Virgin Mary was taken from that evil tree of condemned destruction [Col. 0675C] and sanctified. Although from her mother’s womb she received fullness of grace and holiness, nevertheless, at the conception of the Word, the Holy Spirit coming upon her poured into her more abundantly and more copiously the fullness of heavenly grace, as is evident from the angel’s words. “Hail, Mary, full of grace” [Note: [Col. 0675] Luc. 1.]: behold the fullness of grace. “The Holy Spirit will come upon you” [Note: [Col. 0675] Ibid.]: behold a measure overfull and overflowing.

Therefore, because Mary’s flesh was freed from sin and she herself received grace by measure, she is called blessed not simply, but “among women” [Note: [Col. 0675] Ibid.]. Christ, however, because he possessed grace not by measure and was altogether free and exempt from sin, receives blessing simply: “Blessed,” he says, “is the fruit of your womb” [Note: [Col. 0675] Ibid.]. Mary’s flesh [Col. 0675D] was sanctified; Christ’s flesh was not sanctified, but holy and sanctifying.

This difference of holiness in the flesh was signified by the two tithes of the Old Testament. The children of Israel gave tithes of all their goods to the Levites; but the Levites gave tithes of the best things to the high priest. Thus, from the mass of human flesh—as from a whole body of crops by way of a first tithe—Mary’s flesh was taken out and sanctified [Col. 0676A]; and from that most holy flesh a certain still worthier and holier small portion was chosen, which the Word of God might assume for himself in living flesh. This is the tenth of an ephah, which in Leviticus is commanded to be offered to the Lord as a libation [Note: [Col. 0675] Levit. 6.]. An ephah is a tenth part of a cor. A cor contains thirty measures; an ephah contains three measures, and this is the tenth part of a cor. Thus a tenth of a cor is an ephah, and this is Mary’s flesh. A tenth of an ephah is Christ’s flesh, and it is offered to the Lord as a libation and a sacrifice of sweet fragrance.

Ruth also prefigured this [Note: [Col. 0675] Ruth. 22.]: after she had gathered ears in the field of Boaz, she shook out what she had gathered and found an ephah—that is, three measures. The patriarchs and prophets had foreknown the birth of this Virgin and that Christ would be born from her; longing for this, they devoted themselves to generation. For this reason Hosea [Col. 0676B] took Gomer, a harlot, as wife [Note: [Col. 0675] Ose. 1.]; Isaiah begot his son Jasub [Note: [Col. 0675] Isai. 7.]; Manoah, Samson [Note: [Col. 0675] Judic. 7.]; Elkanah, Samuel [Note: [Col. 0675] I Reg. 1.]; David, Solomon [Note: [Col. 0675] II Reg. 12.]. The mouths of the prophets were opened; innumerable visions occurred, as the Lord says through Hosea: “I multiplied visions, and through the prophets I was represented by likenesses” [Note: [Col. 0675] Ose. 12.]. Not only by words or visions, but by writings, signs, and miracles, the birth both of Christ and of Mary is signified.

If anyone wished to set all these forth, neither tongue nor time would suffice; nor could the capacity of human memory or the patience of ears sustain it. One man and one woman harmed us enormously; but thanks be to God, because through one woman all things have been restored to us, and not without a manifold return of graces. “For the gift is not as the trespass” [Col. 0676C]; rather, the greatness of the benefits exceeds the measure of the harm.

“Sin indeed came from one unto condemnation; but the gift, from many trespasses, unto justification.” The most wise craftsman did not destroy what had been made in Adam, but remade it; he did not break the bruised reed or quench the smoking flax [Note: [Col. 0675] Matth. 12.], but, forming the new Adam from the old, remade the mother in the daughter. Now, Adam, every ground for complaint against a wife has been taken away from you. Do not say: “The woman whom you gave me deceived me and gave me of the forbidden fruit, and I ate” [Note: [Col. 0675] Gen. 3.]; but say: “When I had been cast out from light into darkness, this woman whom you gave me did not deceive me, but gave me of the blessed fruit.” Truly blessed: in it and from it come every [Col. 0676D] blessing, every consolation, and, to use the Apostle’s phrase, every justification, sanctification, and redemption [Note: [Col. 0675] I Cor. 10.].

Behold the house which Wisdom built. Behold Solomon’s litter, the king’s throne, the judge’s tribunal, mercy’s reclining-seat, the propitiatory of being heard, the pattern of instruction, the way of counsel, the end of exile, the abolition of sin, the cancellation of the bond, the assurance of reward, the ladder to heaven, the gate of paradise, the end of figures, the fulfillment of the law, the clarification of the prophets, the manifestation [Col. 0677A] of truth, the exemplar of humility, the safeguard of religion, the school of virtues, the consummation of holiness.

O holy one, O blessed one: you are the moon in the midst of the firmament, the lampstand in the midst of the world, the tree of life in the midst of paradise. Great is your glory in your salvation. Who shall recount your praises? Who shall speak of your mighty deeds? Though the daughters of Zion exalt you, though queens praise you, though your praise is in the Gospel and the prophets, and though the entire Church of the saints proclaims your praise, yet all proclamations and all praises, compared with your blessedness, are like a little torch beside the sun, like a drop beside the vastness of the sea. Amid all our miseries and distresses, you are more ready, more powerful, and more effective than all others for every help and counsel; more worthy of honor, more lovable, [Col. 0677B] more gracious, and sweeter than all. You are sweet in the mouth of those who praise you, in the heart of those who love you, and in the memory of those who entreat you. You have been magnified in every sex, every age, every condition, among tribes, peoples, and languages. You are chosen myrrh; the pool at Heshbon; a little column of smoke from spices; a bundle of myrrh between the breasts of the bridegroom; a terebinth spreading branches of grace and salvation: blessed among all, and super-blessed, supremely chosen, supremely beautiful, supremely gracious, supremely glorious mother of him who gives grace and glory, honor and eternity, to whom be honor and glory for ages of ages. Amen.

## SERMON XXXIX. ON SAINT MICHAEL AND THE GUARDIANSHIP OF ANGELS

[Col. 0677C]

“Deal graciously, O Lord, in your good will with Zion, that the walls of Jerusalem may be built” [Note: [Col. 0677] Psal. 50.].

If we recall the times of Nebuchadnezzar, of Sennacherib, and also of Titus and Vespasian, we do not doubt that earthly Zion was many times captured, destroyed, and rebuilt. And, lest we need go back to ancient histories, the destruction of that city in the time of Pope Urban II, while Philip was king of the Franks, is readily at hand. But now, because our sins have demanded it, this most recent capture and destruction took place under Pope Urban III and another Philip, king of the Franks.

But there is another Jerusalem, the heavenly one, which is our mother. Its walls fell, in no small part, in the ruin and fall of Lucifer and his accomplices [Col. 0677D]. It was the counsel of the Most High that this city should be rebuilt from human beings, as from rational and living stones; and although that counsel had been hidden from the ages, it was nevertheless revealed in the Spirit to the prophets. Hence Daniel and Amos said: “The Lord will do nothing unless he first reveals it to his servants the prophets” [Note: [Col. 0677] Amos 3.].

Therefore the prophet David, aware of this secret and understanding that Jerusalem, signified by Zion, was to be rebuilt from contemplative persons [Col. 0678A], intercedes with the kindness of the supreme Judge in humble and devout prayer. “You, O Lord,” he says, “who have decreed to do good to those whose inward eyes are fixed upon you, just as the eyes of servants are upon the hands of their lord [Note: [Col. 0677] Psal. 122.], do good, O Lord, in your good will to Zion” [Note: [Col. 0677] Psal. 50.], to those who turn toward you the eyes of contemplation and desire. And expressing the manner of this benefit, he adds: “that the walls of Jerusalem may be built.”

Let us, brethren, give thanks to the Most High, because “the Lord takes pleasure in those who fear him, and in them,” etc. [Note: [Col. 0677] Psal. 146.]. He is pleased that the fallen angels’ ruin should be repaired from us, who are enemies: that where the proud one fell, the humble may be raised up; for the ruins of Jerusalem cannot be restored from the angels who transgressed. Indeed, they themselves cannot be restored, because their iniquity “has been found unto hatred” [Col. 0678B]. “There fell those who work iniquity; they were cast out and could not stand” [Note: [Col. 0677] Psal. 35.].

May the Lord, I pray, raise angels from enemies; may he raise the needy from the earth, lifting the poor from the dust, that he may seat him with princes [Note: [Col. 0677] Psal. 112.] and let him possess a throne of glory. “May your kingdom come, O Lord” [Note: [Col. 0677] Matth. 6.]; may the wedding-feast of those reclining at table be filled; may the number of our brothers be completed—I call the angels our brothers, namely our household companions and fellow citizens. Raise up your throne, Lord, in glory, and deign to fill the ruins of your temple from those who are beneath you. For thus, Lord, you spoke through the mouth of your holy prophets from of old [Note: [Col. 0677] Luc. 1.]. Among them Isaiah not only spoke or wrote, but saw “a throne high and lifted up” [Note: [Col. 0677] Isai. 6.]: high in the angels who stood firm [Col. 0678C], lifted up in human beings who ascend by the ladder of divine mercy.

And when that same prophet spoke of the majesty of the Lord which filled the whole earth, he added: “And those things which were beneath him filled the temple” [Note: [Col. 0677] Ibid.]. For the earth of our body, now given into the hands of the wicked, will one day be freed from slavery to sin and from the debt of death: when the Lord saves the humble people and humbles the eyes of the proud [Note: [Col. 0677] Psal. 17.]; when he has shaken off the yoke of the burden and the rod of the taskmaster, whom the Lord will kill with the rod of his mouth; when he has been destroyed and blown away like dust which the wind casts from the face of the earth. Then the Lord will renew the face of our earth, because “this mortal shall put on immortality” [Note: [Col. 0677] I Cor. 15.], and the Lord will reform the body of our lowliness, conforming it [Col. 0678D] to the body of his glory [Note: [Col. 0677] Philipp. 3.]. Thus our earth will be filled with divine majesty [Note: [Col. 0677] Psal. 71.], and then, as it is written, “those things which were beneath him shall fill the temple.” For those who are subject to God in humility will be taken into the angels’ place and fill the ruin of the heavenly temple.

That most lost one refused to be under God; but, wishing to usurp a likeness to divine power, he set up for himself a throne of pestilence in the sides of the north and fell; nor shall he rise again. “For the bed is too narrow, so that one must fall off.” But the fall [Col. 0679A] of one became the ruin of many, for he drew many with him into the same wickedness. Others saw the thief and ran with him, and placed their portion with the adulterer.

Was he not a thief, who deceitfully seized what was not his own but another’s? And when he exalted himself into pride, forgetting the law of life and discipline, he became an adulterer. As the Apostle says: “If you are without discipline, then you are adulterers” [Note: [Col. 0679] Hebr. 12.]. Had that unhappy one been subject to the Lord, he would now be among God’s household, among powers and thrones, among the princes of paradise. He had not yet labored—why, then, was he preparing to sit? Without doubt those will sit who have labored for Christ. “You shall sit upon twelve seats,” etc. [Note: [Col. 0679] Matth. 19.]. But then the miserable one will stand to be judged.

The unhappy one disdained [Col. 0679B] to minister to him for whom to serve is to reign. Certainly those who stood firm in the truth glory in his service, whose face they always behold. For, according to the Apostle, who as a familiar of the heavenly spirits deserved to be present at that supercelestial court, “all are ministering spirits, sent in service for those who receive the inheritance of salvation” [Note: [Col. 0679] Hebr. 1.]. “Thousands of thousands stood before him, and ten thousand times a hundred thousand ministered to him” [Note: [Col. 0679] Dan. 7.].

He who created angels, and who inherited a name so much more excellent than theirs [Note: [Col. 0679] Hebr. 1.] as the Creator is greater than the angel of God, not only deigned to be made a little lower than angels [Note: [Col. 0679] Hebr. 2.], but also freely assumed among sinful and poor human beings the office of a minister. But that son [Col. 0679C] of pride, who in pride and arrogance sought the throne of pestilence, was deposed, so that another might receive his episcopate; and so that a beggar and a poor person might be taken up to the riches of glory which he lost by divine judgment.

“Shall not my soul be subject to God?” If perhaps God may look upon the humility of his handmaid, I shall humble my eyes before the eyes of the Lord; I shall put my mouth in the dust, if perhaps there may be hope [Note: [Col. 0679] Thren. 3.]. I know that God knows our frame [Note: [Col. 0679] Psal. 102.]. We cannot hide our iniquities from him who searches Jerusalem with lamps [Note: [Col. 0679] Soph. 1.], who searches hearts and kidneys [Note: [Col. 0679] Psal. 7.], who finds perversity even in his own angels [Note: [Col. 0679] Job. 4.]. O how blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven and whose sins are covered! [Note: [Col. 0679] Psal. 31.] These are they, Lord, whom you have chosen and taken up; these shall dwell in your courts [Note: [Col. 0679] Psal. 64.]. [Col. 0679D] The sinner will be removed, lest he see the glory of God; but these shall dwell in the abundance of peace.

O most unhappy Lucifer—now no longer *lucifer*, “light-bearer,” but *noctifer*, “night-bearer”—see how, to your disgrace, the Lord today creates from those who are earth, ash, and food for worms, not angels only but seraphim; so that the increase of honor granted to the humble may become for you, the proud, an accumulation of confusion and added pain. Are they not seraphim who, while they are on earth and ash, forget earthly conduct and are inwardly [Col. 0680A] set ablaze by the fire of divine love? “I came,” says the Lord, “to cast fire upon the earth; and what do I desire but that it should burn?” [Note: [Col. 0679] Luc. 12.] The Lord desires that we burn with the fire of love and become seraphim by burning. For *seraphim* is interpreted “burning ones.” That Lucifer wished only to shine, not to burn. Had he burned while shining, he would not have been cold, nor would he have set up his throne in the cold region.

Even now many have contracted something of the wickedness of the fallen angel, desiring to shine rather than to burn. For one shines and does not burn who, under the pretense of feigned religion, is lifted up by the breeze of popular renown. Such a person, like the moon, because he has no heat, borrows his light from elsewhere. Thus, according to the testimony of the Wise Man: “The fool changes like the moon, but the wise person remains like the sun” [Note: [Col. 0679] Eccli. 27.]. The present life is a matter of burning, not shining; therefore the fire must be kindled [Col. 0680B] and nourished on the altar of the heart, as is read in Leviticus [Note: [Col. 0679] Cap. 6.]. But there “the righteous shall shine like the sun in the presence of their Father” [Note: [Col. 0679] Matth. 13.]. It is better to burn here than to shine: Lucifer shone and fell; the seraph burned and stood, because “love never falls away” [Note: [Col. 0679] I Cor. 12.].

You know, brothers, that the angels are joined to God in very close familiarity; and yet through the grace of him who made both them and us, they have become our companions and fellow citizens. Nevertheless, since they belong to the school of him who loves peace and truth; since they are angels of peace, sons of peace, citizens and princes of that Jerusalem whose “participation is in the same thing” [Note: [Col. 0679] Psal. 121.], they demand from us above all things peace, concord [Col. 0680C], and mutual love. Desiring for himself the peace of the angelic fellowship, and urging it upon us, the apostle Peter says: “Above all, have continual mutual love,” [Note: [Col. 0679] I Petr. 4.] etc. And again: “Love one another, not in word nor in tongue, but in deed and truth” [Note: [Col. 0679] I Joan. 3.].

It is expedient for us, brothers, that, just as among angels there is mutual love and ready reverence toward God, so among us there may be one heart and one soul, and toward the shepherd devout obedience and humble service. The Lord’s tunic is seamless [Note: [Col. 0679] Joan. 19.] and undivided. The angels have been clothed in it, and angelic men ought to be clothed in it. Know, moreover, that whoever separates himself from the union of brotherly love by sign, word, or deed tears the Lord’s tunic. “Think the same thing,” says the Apostle, “and let there be no schisms among you” [Note: [Col. 0679] I Cor. 1.].

When in Abraham’s sacrifice spiritual persons were represented by birds and secular persons by animals, Abraham [Note: [Col. 0679] Gen. 15.], at the Lord’s command, divided the heifer and the ram and placed the divided portions opposite one another, but did not divide the dove and the turtledove [Col. 0680D].

I do not speak of pride. But I beseech you—indeed, insofar as I may, I excommunicate and condemn it—that pride may not even be named among you. The malice of pride has been found worthy of eternal hatred. That heavenly city was once disturbed by this plague and partly [Col. 0681A] destroyed. Its citizens abominably abhor pride; nor does anyone share angelic fellowship unless he has humbled himself like a little child. Nor does the Lord rest except upon one who is humble and gentle and trembles at his words [Note: [Col. 0681] Isa. 66.].

Indeed, the Angel did nothing; he merely conceived pride, and in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, he was cast down [Note: [Col. 0681] I Cor. 15.]. Pride changed an angel into a devil, a prince of light into a prince of darkness. Therefore do not be proud, man, since you are earth, ash, and most worthless dust, to be scattered into nothing by a slight breath. If we wish to become companions of angels, let us humble ourselves beneath God’s mighty hand. The humbler we are, the more pleasing we shall be to the angels; humility is akin to them, for when others fell in their pride, these stood firm in their humility [Col. 0681B].

Just as angels are concerned for the rebuilding of their city, so they are attentive to the pursuit of our salvation; for that rebuilding is our salvation. Therefore our tears, burning compunctions, anxious groans, secret rejoicings, devout prayers, the guarding of chastity, the observance of obedience, contempt for temporal things, and perseverance in voluntary poverty please them. These are the sacrifices; these are the incenses which they offer to the Lord for us. Since we do not have as intimate an access to the height of divine majesty as angels do, they faithfully present our prayers to the Lord. Thus, after Scripture had said, “Many incenses were given to him,” it added: “And the smoke of the spices ascended from [Col. 0681C] the hand of the Angel into the presence of the Lord” [Note: [Col. 0681] Apoc. 8.].

Let us, dearest brothers, honor the Lord’s angels in every way as friends and members of God’s household, so that they too may honor us and receive us into eternal dwellings: into the restoration of the heavenly Jerusalem, the filling of the heavenly temple, and the building of Christ’s body. May the Lord of angels deign to grant this to us through the merits of the angels, he to whom belong honor and glory for ages of ages. Amen.

## SERMON XL. ON THE SAME FEAST

“Many incenses were given to him; and the smoke of the spices ascended into the presence of God from the hand of the angel” [Note: [Col. 0681] Ibid.].

John in the Apocalypse speaks of the ministry of the angels [Col. 0681D], who are concerned for our salvation for a threefold reason: for our sake, for God’s sake, and for their own. For our sake, because they recognize their own nature in our souls, which are rational spirits; and they understand that we are joined to them by conformity of nature and, so to speak, by a certain kinship, because we share in and are capable of blessedness and eternal glory. For God’s sake, whose tender mercies they see poured out upon us. “For no one has greater love than to lay down [Col. 0682A] his life for his friends” [Note: [Col. 0681] John 15.]. They know that he loved us—not because we loved him, as John says [Note: [Col. 0681] I John 4.], but because he first loved us and gave his life for us.

It is a common saying: “Whoever loves me, loves my dog as well.” Would that we too were dogs and licked our wounds! Or at least little dogs, so that we might eat of the crumbs falling from the table of our masters. For they themselves are our masters—or rather, the dominions and principalities of heaven—who sit at the table of the Most High, where they are satisfied from the abundance of God’s house and given drink from the torrent of eternal delight. They rejoice and exult in blessings which “eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor have entered into the heart of man” [Note: [Col. 0681] I Cor. 2.]. They are satisfied with the fat of wheat; we, however, with a kind of bran and with the outer husk of the sacrament.

[Col. 0682B] They love us for their own sake, because from us—namely, as from rational and living stones—the ruin of their city and the collapse of the heavenly walls must be rebuilt. This is the threefold cord by which we are drawn by the angels: that we may be God’s building and grow into a holy temple of the Lord. Let us reverence them, brethren, because they are most necessary to us. For they are God’s household and intimates, citizens of heaven, and princes of paradise. They are our lords and our servants: servants in attendance, lords in protection. They are those who minister to God on our behalf.

The Apostle Paul also [Note: [Col. 0681] II Cor. 12.], caught up into the third heaven, saw their ministry while he was present in that heavenly court. And he who saw it bore testimony, [Col. 0682C] saying that “they are all ministering spirits, sent for service on behalf of those who are to inherit salvation” [Note: [Col. 0681] Heb. 1.]. They carry to God our prayers and petitions, hidden sighs, anxious groans, burning compunctions, jubilations, secrets, and the other desires of devotion by which the penitent soul pours itself out like water before the Lord; and they bring back to us the benefits of his mercy. These are the incenses which from the angel’s hand send forth the smoke of perfumes in God’s sight. What is the smoke of perfumes but the devotion of prayers? “Let my prayer rise like incense before you” [Note: [Col. 0681] Ps. 140].

Do not wonder that angels minister where the Lord of angels ministers. For he himself says, “I came to minister, not to be ministered to, and to lay down [Col. 0682D] my life for many” [Note: [Col. 0681] Matt. 20]. In order to minister to us, he made himself a little lower than the angels [Note: [Col. 0681] Heb. 2]. He was indeed made lower through the humility of his dispensation, while remaining greater through the glory of his majesty [Note: [Col. 0681] John 1]. Thus angels ascend and descend upon the Son of Man; thus, according to the Song, the bridegroom comes to the bride, “leaping upon the mountains and skipping over the hills” [Note: [Col. 0681] Cant. 2]. Therefore the citizens of heaven minister, and the Lord of heaven ministers to us as well.

But that Lucifer, who rose in the morning, refused to minister; and therefore he fell. His covering was [Col. 0683A] every precious stone, as Ezekiel testifies [Note: [Col. 0683] Ch. 28.], because he excelled all the other angels. And, as the same Ezekiel says, he was “the seal of likeness, full of knowledge and perfect in beauty, amid the delights of God’s paradise” [Note: [Col. 0683] Ibid.]. Yet, according to blessed Job’s testimony, “he was the beginning of the ways of God” [Note: [Col. 0683] Job 40]; but he was cast down and thrown out, because in his pride and arrogance he thought to ascend the mountain of the covenant and set his throne upon the sides of the north.

The others ministered and stood, as it is written: “The cherubim stood above it; thousands of thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times a hundred thousand stood before him” [Note: [Col. 0683] Dan. 7]. But he, shameless and senseless, would not sit. His imitators are those who flee labour and seek honours. “They are not in the labour of men, nor are they scourged with men” [Note: [Col. 0683] Ps. 72]. [Col. 0683B] For they await labour and pain and everlasting scourges with the demons.

Why, man—ash and dust—do you not attend? Why do you not consider how much danger ambition for power involves? “I saw Satan,” he says, “falling like lightning from heaven” [Note: [Col. 0683] Luke 10]. O proud and malicious spirit: because you would not stand and minister before the Lord, you will yet see human beings sitting upon twelve thrones, and there you will stand before them to be judged. “Do you not know,” says the Apostle, “that we shall judge angels?” [Note: [Col. 0683] I Cor. 6].

Brethren, we are bound to render every reverence and every service of devoted dependents to the angels, as God’s intimates and counsellors, our helpers and defenders. They reconcile us to God; they drive away our enemies; they stir up our devotions; they obtain grace for us, [Col. 0683C] and excuse the excesses of our weakness. But just as they rejoice over a sinner doing penance, so they abhor and flee those whom they see persisting stubbornly in their sins and prolonging the time of repentance. For what fellowship has light with darkness, the sinner with the angel, the carnal person sold under sin with the spirit? Can those please angels who sit in their own filth and drink the urine of their sins, whose thoughts and deeds stink in the nostrils of angels?

The angels are scandalized and withdraw, so that the one left behind may say: “My friends and neighbours came near and stood against me; and those who were near me stood afar off. Therefore those who sought my life used violence” [Note: [Col. 0683] Ps. 37]. “You have removed friend and neighbour far from me, and my acquaintances because of misery” [Note: [Col. 0683] Ps. 87]. “Woe to the man through whom scandal comes” [Note: [Col. 0683] Matt. 18]. If it is dangerous to scandalize one of these little ones, how much more dangerous is it to scandalize one or many of those angels? Woe to that man through whom scandal comes! No one is excepted, whether he scandalizes an angel, a little one, or any neighbour.

But you say: “The angel is bound to love me for [Col. 0684A] God’s sake, for our sake, and for his own, as was stated above.” Can an angel love for God’s sake a person whom he sees opposed and rebellious to God? Nor will they love a person in whom they see a spirit falling away from conformity with angelic power; nor, for their own sake or for the rebuilding of their city, will they love those who ought to have been living stones but have become “like dust which the wind drives from the face of the earth” [Note: [Col. 0683] Ps. 1], lacking that by which they were to be joined and built together with the angels: the bond of love and the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.

Woe to the man through whom scandal comes! There is an outward scandal, by which the little one is offended, the mature person troubled, and the angel driven away. There is also a scandal that we suffer inwardly, when we feel a contrary law [Col. 0684B] in our members; and this is the scandal of eye, hand, and foot. The inner eye scandalizes us when our intention subjects itself to some improper pleasure. But you have the counsel to pluck out this eye and cast it from you [Note: [Col. 0683] Matt. 18]: that is, let the will be rejected lest it arrive at consent.

At times, concerning a good work, the affection of our understanding troubles us with evil concern. This is the scandal of the hand; and you cut it off if you do not consent as far as the actual performance of the deed. If you were advancing toward what is better, ascending from step to step by Jacob’s ladder, if your foot stood straight, beware lest the foot of pride move you. For if your steps are disturbed or poured out, so that through sloth and a certain weariness you begin to grow sluggish in the Lord’s way, know that [Col. 0684C] your inner foot scandalizes you. Therefore, by the Saviour’s counsel, cut off your foot, that you may run more freely in the way of heavenly commandments.

Do not be occupied with various desires or actions. He who is everywhere is nowhere; he who directs himself to many things advances in few. Yet “one thing is necessary” [Note: [Col. 0683] Luke 10]. It is better to enter the kingdom of heaven with one foot or one eye than, having two eyes or two feet, to be cast into the hell of fire [Note: [Col. 0683] Matt. 18]. “My son, let not your activities be many,” says the Wise Man [Note: [Col. 0683] Ecclus. 11]. “The ark was completed in one cubit” [Note: [Col. 0683] Gen. 6]. Woe to the man walking by two ways [Note: [Col. 0683] Ecclus. 3]! “For he who walks simply walks securely” [Note: [Col. 0683] Prov. 30].

Simplicity plainly removes the scandal of the foot. And if you act simply and cut off malicious desires, you remove the scandal of eye and hand. For if your eye [Col. 0684D] is single—that is, your intention in acting—your whole body of works and thoughts will be full of light, and your works will shine before men, that they may glorify your Father who is in heaven [Note: [Col. 0683] Matt. 6]. Then you will attain grace and glory before God and his angels. May he deign to grant this to us all through the ministry of angels—to whom be honour and glory for ages of ages. Amen.

## SERMON XLI. ON THE FEAST OF ALL SAINTS

[Col. 0685A]

“Our soul has been delivered like a sparrow from the snare of those who hunt; the snare has been broken, and we have been set free” [Note: [Col. 0685] Ps. 123].

This whole verse—indeed, this whole psalm—is an act of thanksgiving and a voice of praise. For the saints whose feast is celebrated today formerly inhabited frail houses of clay like ourselves, and in the body of this death they severely experienced the snares of temptation and the malice of the enemy. But now, because the Lord has led their souls out of the dangers of this life, the Prophet speaks in their person and says: “Our soul, like [Col. 0685B] a sparrow,” and so forth.

The saying which John gives in the Apocalypse accords and agrees with this: “Under God’s altar I heard the voice of the slain saying: ‘Avenge, Lord, the blood of your servants which has been shed’” [Note: [Col. 0685] Apoc. 6]. This is not the voice of those awaiting vengeance, but of those desiring the glorification of their bodies. For the souls which have departed from bodies are placed under God’s altar and joyfully await, in tranquil rest, the second robe—that is, the glorification of the body.

The holy Fathers understand God’s altar as Christ’s glorified body. For a time, the souls’ delight consists in beholding it, until the number of their brethren is fulfilled. These are the eagles that gather to the body. As it is written: “Wherever the body may be, there the eagles will gather” [Note: [Col. 0685] Matt. 24]. Thus they delight in the sight of [Col. 0685C] glorified flesh in Christ, who now grants them the robe of the soul and will at last grant them the glorification of the body; and in this rest they await the glory of complete glorification. Hence the voice which says: “The righteous await me, until you reward me” [Note: [Col. 0685] Ps. 141].

Certainly, those awaiting the glorification of the body received the divine response given them in the Apocalypse: “Wait a little while, until the number of your brethren is fulfilled” [Note: [Col. 0685] Apoc. 6]. For it is written concerning the patriarchs and prophets: “God having provided something better for us, that they should not be made perfect without us” [Note: [Col. 0685] Heb. 11].

Indeed, at the moment when a person’s soul leaves the prison of this body and stands, as it were, at the gate by which one departs from this life, it passes, according to the measure of its works, to joys [Col. 0685D] or pains, according to the saying, “Their works follow them” [Note: [Col. 0685] Apoc. 14]. But the righteous person “will not be confounded when he speaks with his enemies in the gate” [Note: [Col. 0685] Ps. 126]. For it will be said of him: “Give him from the fruit of his hands, and let his works praise him in the gates” [Note: [Col. 0685] Prov. 31]. And although they have been in labours, from henceforth the Spirit tells them to rest from their labours [Note: [Col. 0685] Apoc. 14].

Formerly, indeed, all descended to hell. Hence blessed Job says: “Who will grant me that you protect me in hell and hide me until your wrath passes, and appoint me a time when [Col. 0686A] you will remember me?” [Note: [Col. 0685] Job 14]. Yet a great chasm had been fixed between the righteous and the wicked. For the righteous sat in Abraham’s bosom—that is, rested in darkness—awaiting the blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of the great God.
